magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mostly aligned with the Catholic understanding of a serious, gradual preparation for marriage: it encourages the engaged couple toward honest conversation, self-knowledge, and responsible discernment, rather than mere formal attendance of the course. It does not set forth teaching that would contradict Sacred Scripture, although it mostly portrays marriage psychologically and practically, without explicit mention of its sacramental and religious meaning.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic preparation for marriage is not just a communication course, but preparation for a vocation and a sacrament: the Church emphasizes that marriage shares in Christ's love for the Church and that the maturity of this vocation requires proper and specific preparation. The time of engagement is therefore suitable for discussion on freedom of consent, the unity and indissolubility of marriage, sexuality, responsible parenthood, and the upbringing of children; ecclesial documents also describe preparation as a path that continues through family life.
concerns_en: The claim that “I do” completely transforms two people and creates something new should be understood as a description of the emergence of the marital communion and a new vocation in life, rather than as a claim that the personality, history, or personal responsibility of the spouses disappear.

The passage does not explicitly mention that Christian marriage is a sacrament, nor its essential dimensions such as free consent, fidelity, indissolubility, and openness to life; this is a limitation of the presented content, rather than a direct error.

sections.subtitle_en: Investing before day one: why one weekend lecture is not enough
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel describes the seven-meeting marriage preparation course run by Fokus
sections.content_en:
Kruno asks whether it pays off to invest in marriage even before its beginning, during the engagement. He states that he knows many couples whom premarital counseling helped and prevented problems in marriage from multiplying.

Daniel answers affirmatively and refers to his own experience. Although he and Kate thought they knew each other well, the course opened up topics about which they had not spoken or which were no longer on their radar. That is why he encourages young people to choose a **good premarital course**. Some complained to him that the course where they live comes down to one or two lectures over a weekend. Daniel considers that to be too little, because in such a short time one cannot even open one's own questions and doubts.

The marriage preparation course led by Daniel and Kate has **six plus one, that is, seven meetings**, and lasts two to three months. In that span, a couple manages to reflect more deeply on questions, and even argue, and discover what really bothers them and what still needs to be talked about.

The biggest mistake of young people is that they complete the course just so others would see that they attended. That way they get the least out of it. Daniel calls on them to take the course seriously and give themselves the best opportunity to prepare. Nevertheless, he emphasizes that for marriage **no one can prepare completely**. The fateful “I do” completely transforms two people and creates something new, although personalities and histories remain the same. What can be done is to get to know oneself and the other person as best as possible: what one likes, what one prefers, and what kind of **baggage** one carries from family, values, and upbringing. A longer course gives space for that baggage to be unpacked.

sections.subtitle: Ubojice veze i trik s kaučem: nismo mi problem, problem je naš
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel pokazuje razliku između sjedenja licem u lice i gledanja u istom smjeru
sections.content:
Kruno pita koje su najčešće „ubojice” veze i braka. Daniel odgovara da se parovi, bez obzira na temu, najviše svađaju zbog **nedostatka dobre i kvalitetne komunikacije**. Previše čitaju između redova, pretpostavljaju umjesto da provjere i nose razočarana očekivanja koja se nisu ispunila jer nisu bila jasno izrečena. Često nije presudno što je problem, nego **kako mu se pristupilo** i jesu li partneri mogli dobro razgovarati.

**Gledati u istom smjeru**

Daniel prenosi savjet koji su on i Kate nedavno isprobali na jednom programu, gdje su više sudjelovali nego moderirali. Kad pred parom stoji težak razgovor, partneri ne bi trebali sjediti jedan nasuprot drugome, kao Daniel i Kruno u studiju. Bolje je sjesti na kauč i okrenuti se u istom smjeru. Govor tijela tada poručuje: *nisam protiv tebe, nego zajedno gledamo u naš problem i tražimo rješenje.* Bilo da je riječ o novcu, djeci ili roditeljima, par tako lakše vidi da je problem zajednički, a da oni sami nisu problem.

Daniel i Kate kod kuće često idu u **šetnju** kad trebaju razgovarati o nekom problemu. Šetnja ih prisiljava da oboje gledaju naprijed, razgovaraju i mole. Nakon pola sata nisu sve riješili, ali su izbjegli međusobne napade i stalnu potrebu za obranom. Možda još nisu došli do zaključka, ali su se čuli, a to je prvi korak.

Na Krunovu šalu o deset tisuća koraka Daniel odgovara da ih je prije pet tisuća. Dodaje da takva šetnja znači i zajedničko vrijeme i svjež zrak, kao i svjesnu odluku da se radi na odnosu. Priznaje da je sklon guranju stvari pod tepih. Šetnja ga primora da progovori, jer zna zašto su izašli i ne može samo šutjeti. Tako oboje dobivaju **fer podlogu** da se čuju i dobro razgovaraju.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim razumijevanjem bračnog dijaloga: potiče jasnoću, pažljivo slušanje, izbjegavanje optuživanja i zajedničko traženje rješenja. Ideja da supružnici zajedno gledaju na problem može dobro izraziti bračnu solidarnost, a zajednička molitva dodatno podsjeća da kršćanski brak nije samo ljudski projekt nego zajednički put pred Bogom.
concerns: Poruka da je „problem naš, a ne mi sami” korisna je kao način izbjegavanja međusobnog suprotstavljanja, ali ne bi smjela značiti da se zanemaruju osobna odgovornost, istina ili potreba za isprikom i oprostom.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko učenje cijeni dijalog kao bitan dio ljubavi u braku te naglašava strpljivo slušanje, pažljiv izbor riječi i izbjegavanje govora koji vrijeđa ili ponižava. Šetnja ili sjedenje okrenuto u istom smjeru mogu biti praktična pomagala za takav razgovor, ali nisu sama po sebi duhovno rješenje: važno je da supružnici nastave tražiti pomirenje, a molitva može osnažiti njihovu bračnu povezanost.

citations.document_title: Holy Mass with the Rite of Marriage (14 September 2014)

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the Catholic understanding of marital dialogue: it encourages clarity, attentive listening, avoiding accusations, and the joint search for solutions. The idea that spouses look at a problem together can well express marital solidarity, and shared prayer additionally reminds that Christian marriage is not just a human project, but a shared journey before God.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching values dialogue as an essential part of love in marriage and emphasizes patient listening, a careful choice of words, and the avoidance of speech that offends or humiliates. A walk or sitting facing the same direction can be practical aids for such a conversation, but they are not in themselves a spiritual solution: it is important that spouses continue to seek reconciliation, and prayer can strengthen their marital bond.
concerns_en: The message that “the problem is ours, and not ourselves” is useful as a way to avoid mutual opposition, but it should not mean that personal responsibility, truth, or the need for apology and forgiveness are neglected.

sections.subtitle_en: Relationship killers and the trick with the couch: we are not the problem, the problem is ours
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel shows the difference between sitting face to face and looking in the same direction
sections.content_en:
Kruno asks what the most common “killers” of a relationship and marriage are. Daniel answers that couples, regardless of the topic, fight the most because of **a lack of good and quality communication**. They read too much between the lines, assume instead of checking, and carry disappointed expectations that were not fulfilled because they were not clearly stated. Often it is not decisive what the problem is, but **how it was approached** and whether the partners were able to have a good conversation.

**Looking in the same direction**

Daniel shares advice that he and Kate recently tried at a program, where they participated more than they moderated. When a couple faces a difficult conversation, the partners should not sit opposite each other, like Daniel and Kruno in the studio. It is better to sit on the couch and face the same direction. Body language then sends the message: *I am not against you, but we are looking at our problem together and seeking a solution.* Whether it is about money, children, or parents, the couple thus more easily sees that the problem is shared, and that they themselves are not the problem.

Daniel and Kate at home often go for a **walk** when they need to talk about a problem. The walk forces them both to look forward, talk, and pray. After half an hour they have not resolved everything, but they have avoided mutual attacks and the constant need for defense. Maybe they have not yet reached a conclusion, but they heard each other, and that is the first step.

To Kruno's joke about ten thousand steps, Daniel replies that it is rather five thousand. He adds that such a walk means both time together and fresh air, as well as a conscious decision to work on the relationship. He admits that he is prone to sweeping things under the rug. The walk forces him to speak up, because he knows why they went out and cannot just remain silent. In this way, both get a **fair ground** to hear each other and talk well.

sections.subtitle: Slušati da bi razumio, a ne da bi odgovorio: „kako to” umjesto „zašto”
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel objašnjava zašto pitanje „zašto” izaziva obranu, a „kako to” otvara razgovor
sections.content:
Kruno traži konkretne savjete za bolju komunikaciju. Daniel kaže da se svi savjeti svode na jednostavne korake, ali da je ključna **unutarnja motivacija** da se čovjek time želi baviti. Glavna su načela da partneri čuju jedno drugo, da se ne prekidaju i ne upadaju si u riječ.

**Slušanje kao obavijest o tuđim manama**

Najveća lekcija, prema Danielu, glasi: **slušati da bi razumio**. Priznaje da u svađi sluša da bi odgovorio. Dok mu Kate govori, on već smišlja obranu. Tada ne sudjeluje u komunikaciji, nego ima „obavijest” za nju: ona ga informira o njegovim manama, a on će nju o njezinima. Tako se ne riješi ništa.

Daniel preporučuje knjige, tečajeve i seminare o komunikaciji. Komunikaciju vidi kao **vještinu koja se razvija**. Nekima ide prirodno, a njemu teže. Cilj nije savršenstvo, nego napredak: tko je na ljestvici od jedan do deset na dvojci, može se truditi doći do trojke.

**Ja-izjave i čarolija dviju riječi**

Među malim pomacima Daniel ističe izjave koje počinju s „ja”, a ne s „ti”, kako bi se izbjeglo optuživanje. Posebno izdvaja jednostavan savjet. Kad partner želi doznati zašto se nešto dogodilo ili nije dogodilo, neka pitanje ne počne sa „zašto”, nego s **„kako to”**. Na pitanje „zašto si kasnio?” prva je reakcija opravdavanje. Na pitanje „kako to da si kasnio?” lako je odgovoriti da je bio sudar ili da nije bilo parkinga, pa razgovor ostaje prijateljski.

Daniel priznaje da i sam pitanje sa „zašto” doživljava kao napad, što Kruno odmah prepoznaje. Tada se gradi zid, a razgovor postaje ping-pong izjava. Ono što jedan kaže drugi doživljava kao izvlačenje i nepreuzimanje odgovornosti. Zato Daniel i sam mora vježbati. Umjesto da pretpostavi da je Kate imala vremena, pita je kako to da nije skuhala ručak. Ona odgovori da ju je netko nazvao i da je morala biti s djecom, i to mu je potpuno u redu.

**Znatiželja umjesto osude**

Ako su partneri **znatiželjni, a ne osuđujući**, odnos trpi puno manje pritiska. Daniel naglašava da su on i Kate dvoje ljudi koji su se odabrali s dobrim namjerama. Pogreške se događaju, ali partneri jedan drugome čuvaju leđa time što **vjeruju u najbolje kod drugoga**.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom snažno usklađen s katoličkim razumijevanjem bračnog dijaloga: strpljivo slušanje, obzirno izražavanje i nastojanje da se drugoga ne tretira kao protivnika izravno odgovaraju naglascima pape Franje u *Amoris laetitia*. Prikaz znatiželje i povjerenja u dobre namjere drugoga dobro se slaže s kršćanskim pozivom na ljubav, premda te stavove treba povezati s iskrenim razgovorom i odgovornim priznavanjem pogrešaka.
concerns: Savjet da se „zašto” zamijeni s „kako to” može biti koristan, ali ne treba ga shvatiti kao univerzalno pravilo: samo pitanje „zašto” nije nužno optužujuće, a blag ton i iskrena namjera važniji su od same formulacije. Povjerenje u najbolje kod partnera također ne bi smjelo značiti prešućivanje povrede ili izbjegavanje odgovornosti.
magisterium.enrichment: Papa Franjo opisuje bračni dijalog kao vještinu koja se razvija te naglašava da supružnici trebaju strpljivo slušati do kraja, ne pripremati odgovor dok drugi govori i nastojati razumjeti njegove brige. Obzirno biranje riječi i otvorenost za drukčije gledište pomažu da razgovor ne postane nadmetanje u kojem je važnije pobijediti nego čuvati zajedništvo. U kršćanskom smislu, povjerenje i blagost ne isključuju istinu: mogu stvoriti sigurniji prostor u kojem se pogreške priznaju i na njima se radi bez ponižavanja druge osobe.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely strongly aligned with the Catholic understanding of marital dialogue: patient listening, considerate expression, and the effort not to treat the other as an opponent directly correspond to the emphases of Pope Francis in *Amoris laetitia*. The depiction of curiosity and trust in the other's good intentions accords well with the Christian call to love, although these attitudes should be connected with honest conversation and responsible acknowledgment of mistakes.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Pope Francis describes marital dialogue as a skill that develops and emphasizes that spouses should listen patiently until the end, not prepare a response while the other is speaking, and strive to understand their concerns. Considerately choosing words and openness to a different perspective help ensure that conversation does not become a competition in which it is more important to win than to preserve communion. In a Christian sense, trust and gentleness do not exclude the truth: they can create a safer space in which mistakes are acknowledged and worked on without humiliating the other person.
concerns_en: The advice to replace "why" with "how come" can be useful, but it should not be taken as a universal rule: the question "why" itself is not necessarily accusatory, and a gentle tone and sincere intention are more important than the formulation itself. Trusting the best in one's partner should also not mean keeping silent about hurt or avoiding responsibility.

sections.subtitle_en: Listening to understand, not to respond: "how come" instead of "why"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel explains why the question "why" provokes defensiveness, and "how come" opens up conversation
sections.content_en:
Kruno asks for concrete advice for better communication. Daniel says that all advice boils down to simple steps, but that the key is the **internal motivation** to want to engage with it. The main principles are for partners to hear each other, not to interrupt each other, and not to cut each other off.

**Listening as a notice of another's flaws**

The greatest lesson, according to Daniel, is: **to listen in order to understand**. He admits that in an argument he listens in order to respond. While Kate is speaking to him, he is already formulating a defense. Then he is not participating in communication, but has a "notice" for her: she informs him of his flaws, and he will inform her of hers. Nothing is resolved that way.

Daniel recommends books, courses, and seminars on communication. He sees communication as a **skill that develops**. For some it comes naturally, and for him with greater difficulty. The goal is not perfection, but progress: whoever is at a two on a scale from one to ten can strive to reach a three.

**"I"-statements and the magic of two words**

Among the small shifts Daniel emphasizes statements that begin with "I" and not with "you", in order to avoid blaming. He particularly singles out a simple piece of advice. When a partner wants to find out why something happened or did not happen, let the question not begin with "why", but with **"how come"**. To the question "why were you late?", the first reaction is making excuses. To the question "how come you were late?", it is easy to answer that there was an accident or that there was no parking, so the conversation remains friendly.

Daniel admits that he himself experiences the question with "why" as an attack, which Kruno immediately recognizes. Then a wall is built, and the conversation becomes a ping-pong of statements. What one says the other perceives as making excuses and not taking responsibility. That is why Daniel must practice himself. Instead of assuming that Kate had time, he asks her how come she did not cook lunch. She answers that someone called her and that she had to be with the children, and that is completely fine with him.

**Curiosity instead of condemnation**

If partners are **curious rather than judgmental**, the relationship suffers much less pressure. Daniel emphasizes that he and Kate are two people who chose each other with good intentions. Mistakes happen, but partners have each other's back by **believing in the best in each other**.

sections.subtitle: Fizičkost kao zamagljene naočale: zašto dodir ne vrijedi tisuću riječi
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel uspoređuje fizičku intimnost s naočalama koje se zamagle pri otvaranju pećnice
sections.content:
Kruno primjećuje da neki parovi svađe rješavaju fizičkom intimnošću. Kad u braku nestane komunikacije, nestane i intimnosti na kojoj su gradili odnos. Pita kako Daniel gleda na intimne potrebe muškarca i žene, uz opasku da je muškarcima to visoko na ljestvici prioriteta, a žene to drukčije doživljavaju.

Daniel kaže da pitanje nije jednostavno. Upozorava na generalizaciju prema kojoj je muškarcima seksualna intimnost bitnija, a ženama nije. Prema njemu, to nije sasvim točno: ženama je jednako važna, samo do nje dolaze **drugim putem**.

**Zamagljivač u vezi**

Na zaručničkim tečajevima Daniel i Kate snažno savjetuju parovima da **„ohlade” od fizičkog**. Fizičkost smatraju jednim od najvećih **„zamagljivača”**, kako ga sami zovu. Daniel to uspoređuje s otvaranjem pećnice, kad se naočale potpuno zamagle. Fizički kontakt je komunikacija koja se odvija kroz tijelo: uzbuđenje, dodir, nježnost. Zbog toga lako nastaje **lažan dojam da se partneri razumiju**. Čini se dovoljnim zagrliti se i poljubiti, a par pritom postaje slijep za pravi problem i prestaje komunicirati. Daniel zaključuje da dodir ne vrijedi tisuću riječi. Svaki supružnik zna koliko toga u svađama ostane neizrečeno, a to se mora adekvatno riješiti.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom jer s pravom upozorava da fizička intimnost ne može zamijeniti iskren razgovor ni razrješavanje sukoba, a suzdržanost tijekom udvaranja može služiti čistoći i razboritom upoznavanju. Ipak, izraz „zamagljivač” i tvrdnja da dodir ne vrijedi tisuću riječi traže pojašnjenje kako ne bi umanjili vrijednost bračne tjelesne nježnosti kao stvarnog izraza ljubavi.
concerns: Katolički nauk ne prikazuje tjelesnu intimnost u braku kao puku smetnju komunikaciji: nježni izrazi i bračno sjedinjenje mogu biti plemeniti znakovi uzajamnog darivanja i pridonijeti ljubavi supružnika. Problem nastaje kada se njima prikriva neriješen sukob, a ne zbog same tjelesnosti.

Tvrdnja da je ženama intimnost jednako važna, ali da do nje dolaze „drugim putem”, može biti korisno opažanje, no ne bi je trebalo pretvarati u univerzalno pravilo o muškarcima i ženama; potrebno je uvažavati osobnost, potrebe i ritam svakog supružnika.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni nauk istodobno vrednuje bračnu tjelesnost i razgovor: bračna ljubav obuhvaća cijelu osobu, a tjelesni izrazi mogu biti posebni znakovi bračnog prijateljstva; zato ih ne treba suprotstavljati riječima, nego povezati s istinom i uzajamnim darivanjem. Papa Franjo također upozorava da spolni čin ne smije biti nametnut te ističe važnost sporazuma supružnika, dok za dijalog preporučuje otvorenost i osjetljivo rješavanje povrijeđenosti. U kontekstu zaručništva poziv na čistoću može biti smislen, ali u braku nježnost i spolno sjedinjenje nisu prepreka bliskosti: mogu je izražavati, dok sami po sebi ne rješavaju svaku nesuglasicu.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching because it rightly warns that physical intimacy cannot replace honest conversation or conflict resolution, and restraint during courtship can serve chastity and prudent mutual discovery. Nevertheless, the term "fogger" and the claim that a touch is not worth a thousand words require clarification so as not to diminish the value of marital bodily tenderness as a genuine expression of love.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching simultaneously values marital physicality and conversation: marital love encompasses the whole person, and bodily expressions can be special signs of marital friendship; therefore, they should not be opposed to words, but connected with truth and mutual self-giving. Pope Francis also warns that the sexual act must not be imposed and emphasizes the importance of mutual agreement between spouses, while for dialogue he recommends openness and sensitive resolution of hurt feelings. In the context of engagement, a call to chastity can be meaningful, but in marriage, tenderness and sexual union are not an obstacle to closeness: they can express it, while in themselves they do not resolve every disagreement.
concerns_en: Catholic teaching does not portray bodily intimacy in marriage as a mere hindrance to communication: tender expressions and marital union can be noble signs of mutual self-giving and contribute to the love of spouses. The problem arises when an unresolved conflict is covered up by them, and not because of physicality itself.

The claim that intimacy is equally important to women, but that they arrive at it "by another path," may be a useful observation, but it should not be turned into a universal rule about men and women; it is necessary to respect the individuality, needs, and rhythm of each spouse.

sections.subtitle_en: Physicality like fogged-up glasses: why a touch is not worth a thousand words
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel compares physical intimacy to glasses that fog up when opening an oven
sections.content_en:
Kruno notes that some couples resolve arguments with physical intimacy. When communication disappears in a marriage, the intimacy on which they built the relationship disappears as well. He asks how Daniel views the intimate needs of a man and a woman, noting that for men this is high on the priority list, while women experience it differently.

Daniel says the question is not simple. He warns against the generalization according to which sexual intimacy is more important to men, and not to women. According to him, that is not entirely accurate: it is just as important to women, they just arrive at it **by another path**.

**The fogger in a relationship**

In marriage preparation courses, Daniel and Kate strongly advise couples to **"cool off" from the physical**. They consider physicality one of the greatest **"foggers"**, as they call it themselves. Daniel compares this to opening an oven, when glasses become completely fogged up. Physical contact is communication that takes place through the body: excitement, touch, tenderness. Because of this, a **false impression that the partners understand each other** easily arises. It seems sufficient to hug and kiss, while the couple becomes blind to the real problem and stops communicating. Daniel concludes that a touch is not worth a thousand words. Every spouse knows how much remains unsaid in arguments, and that must be adequately resolved.

sections.subtitle: Istraživanje koje je iznenadilo: ženama najviše nedostaje muška inicijativa
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel prepričava istraživanje o glavnom razlogu manjka želje kod žena
sections.content:
Daniel spominje istraživanje predstavljeno na konferenciji na kojoj su on i Kate nedavno sudjelovali. Žene su u njemu kao **prvi razlog manjka želje za seksualnom intimnošću** navele **nedostatak muške inicijative**. Daniel priznaje da ga je to iznenadilo, jer je mislio da je to tipično muški odgovor. Muškarci, naime, često žele da žene više iniciraju.

Problem je, objašnjava Daniel, u tome što muškarci inicijativu shvaćaju samo u okviru bračne sobe. Ženama inicijativa znači nešto drugo:

- kako je muž pozdravi ujutro kad odlazi na posao,
- je li joj tijekom dana poslao poruku,
- kakve je volje kad se vrati s posla.

Sve to za ženu je inicijativa koja u njoj pokreće ono što želi pružiti mužu. Daniel ističe da žena svoju nutrinu procesuira kompleksnije od muškarca. Spominje video koji opisuje kao „Istina o dva mozga” ili nešto slično. U njemu je muški mozak prikazan kao niz zasebnih kutija, za posao, financije ili seksualnu intimnost, od kojih se svaka otvara posebno. Kod žene je sve isprepleteno, a Kruno dodaje da je sve povezano. Zato žena ne misli samo na to da muž nije inicirao navečer, nego na to da nije inicirao tijekom dana, da tjednima možda nisu razgovarali ni doživjeli trenutak stvarne povezanosti.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na svakodnevnoj pažnji, emocionalnoj povezanosti i uzajamnom nastojanju supružnika uglavnom je usklađen s katoličkim razumijevanjem braka kao zajednice uzajamne odgovornosti, poštovanja i nesebične ljubavi. Ipak, tvrdnje o tome kako muškarci i žene općenito razmišljaju treba shvatiti kao moguća zapažanja, a ne kao nauk Crkve ili univerzalno pravilo.
concerns: Prikaz muškoga mozga kao odvojenih „kutija”, a ženskoga kao isprepletenog, može pojednostavniti složene individualne razlike i stvoriti stereotipna očekivanja; izneseni ulomak ne pruža osnovu da se to predstavi kao opća istina.

Povezivanje muževe inicijative s time što žena želi pružiti mužu ne bi se smjelo shvatiti kao obveza žene da odgovori seksualnom intimnošću. Katolički nauk odbacuje nametanje seksualnog čina i naglašava obzir prema stanju i opravdanim željama drugoga supružnika.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva uči da supružnici trebaju uzimati u obzir psihologiju, ritam i duhovni napredak drugoga te zajedno razvijati skladan odnos; svakodnevna pažnja zato može biti konkretan izraz bračne ljubavi. Bračna intimnost treba biti ljudski čin uzajamnog darivanja i komunikacije, a ne sredstvo pritiska ili manipulacije; Pavao spominje uzajamni dogovor supružnika, a *Amoris laetitia* izričito odbacuje nametnut čin. Stoga se opis inicijative može korisno razumjeti kao poziv na pažljiviju, obostranu izgradnju bliskosti, uz poštovanje osobnosti i slobode obaju supružnika.

citations.document_title: The Bible and Morality: Biblical Roots of Christian Conduct

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on everyday attentiveness, emotional connection, and the mutual effort of the spouses is largely aligned with the Catholic understanding of marriage as a communion of mutual responsibility, respect, and selfless love. Nevertheless, assertions about how men and women think in general should be understood as possible observations, and not as Church teaching or a universal rule.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church teaches that spouses should take into account the psychology, rhythm, and spiritual progress of the other and together develop a harmonious relationship; everyday attentiveness can therefore be a concrete expression of marital love. Marital intimacy should be a human act of mutual self-giving and communication, not a means of pressure or manipulation; Paul mentions the mutual agreement of the spouses, and *Amoris laetitia* explicitly rejects an imposed act. Therefore, the description of initiative can be usefully understood as an invitation to a more attentive, mutual building of closeness, while respecting the personality and freedom of both spouses.
concerns_en: The depiction of the male brain as separate „boxes”, and the female as intertwined, can oversimplify complex individual differences and create stereotypical expectations; the presented excerpt does not provide a basis for presenting this as a general truth.

Linking the husband's initiative with what the woman wants to provide to the husband should not be understood as an obligation of the woman to respond with sexual intimacy. Catholic teaching rejects the imposition of the sexual act and emphasizes consideration for the condition and legitimate desires of the other spouse.

sections.subtitle_en: Research that surprised: women lack male initiative the most
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel recounts a study on the main reason for the lack of desire in women
sections.content_en:
Daniel mentions a study presented at a conference in which he and Kate recently participated. In it, women cited **the lack of male initiative** as the **number one reason for a lack of desire for sexual intimacy**. Daniel admits that this surprised him, because he thought that was a typically male answer. Men, namely, often want women to initiate more.

The problem, Daniel explains, is that men understand initiative only within the framework of the marital bedroom. To women, initiative means something else:

- how the husband greets her in the morning when he leaves for work,
- whether he sent her a message during the day,
- what mood he is in when he returns from work.

All of this for a woman is initiative that sets in motion within her what she wants to offer her husband. Daniel emphasizes that a woman processes her inner world more complexly than a man. He mentions a video he describes as „The Truth About Two Brains” or something similar. In it, the male brain is depicted as a series of separate boxes, for work, finances, or sexual intimacy, each of which opens separately. With a woman, everything is intertwined, and Kruno adds that everything is connected. That is why a woman does not think only about the fact that her husband did not initiate in the evening, but that he did not initiate during the day, that they perhaps have not spoken for weeks or experienced a moment of real connection.

sections.subtitle: Dublja muška potreba: biti željen, voljen i stalno osvajati suprugu
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel opisuje trenutak kada je shvatio da je njegova potreba dublja od fizičke
sections.content:
Daniel otvoreno govori o vlastitom iskustvu. Kad su djeca bila mala, a supruga umorna i bez volje za bilo čim, pitao se je li normalno da on stalno ima želju, a ona gotovo nikad. Tada je shvatio da i njemu zapravo nedostaje **osjećaj da je željen, voljen i da pripada njoj**. Ne radi se samo o fizičkom činu kojim se „namiri” muškarac s velikom potrebom.

Daniel je uvidio da njegova potreba ide puno dublje. Iako se najčešće izražava kroz bračno zajedništvo, i on želi da ga se supruga sjeti, da mu pošalje poruku i da se veseli kad se vrati kući. Muškarci, zaključuje Daniel, sami sebe zavaravaju kad misle da bi bili sretniji kad bi samo bilo više intime. **Ispunjenje dolazi iz ispunjavajućeg odnosa** s osobom kojoj su rekli „da” zauvijek.

**Osvajanje ne prestaje vjenčanjem**

Muškarac ne može proizvesti ni kontrolirati volju i spremnost svoje supruge. Može je, međutim, **nastaviti osvajati**. Prije braka to je bilo prirodno: čokoladica, cvijet, šetnja parkom ili večera. Nakon osvajanja mnogi zaključe da je posao gotov. Kruno to slikovito opisuje izrekom da „zec više nije u šumi, zec je na ražnju”. Daniel se slaže i dodaje da su **žene stvorene da budu voljene**. Treba samo kreativno pronalaziti nove načine, a Kruno to sažima kao osvajanje iz dana u dan.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim razumijevanjem braka jer naglašava trajnu pažnju, nježnost i međusobno darivanje, a bračnu bliskost ne svodi na zadovoljavanje seksualne potrebe. Ipak, tvrdnja da su žene stvorene da budu voljene može zvučati jednostrano ili stereotipno ako se ne pojasni da su muž i žena pozvani uzajamno ljubiti i primati ljubav.
concerns: Formulacija o ženama stvorenima da budu voljene može se pogrešno shvatiti kao svođenje žene na pasivnu ulogu ili kao tvrdnja da muškarci imaju isključivu ulogu onoga koji voli; katolički nauk naglašava uzajamnu ljubav i uzajamno darivanje supružnika.

Osvajanje supruge ne smije značiti pokušaj da se njezina volja ili seksualna spremnost kontroliraju. Odlomak to izričito poriče, ali bilo bi korisno još jasnije istaknuti poštovanje njezine slobode i stvarnih potreba.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje bračne ljubavi uključuje i emocionalnu bliskost i tjelesnu nježnost, ali ih smješta u uzajamno predanje koje poštuje dostojanstvo oboje; supružnici nisu pozvani samo davati nego i primati ljubav kao dar. Sveto pismo i crkveno tumačenje ženidbene slike naglašavaju da Krist ljubi Crkvu sebedarno, dok se brak ostvaruje u uzajamnoj podložnosti i vjernosti, a ne u jednostranoj dominaciji. Pritom treba izbjegavati pretpostavku da svi muškarci i žene osjećaju ili izražavaju ljubav na isti način: biblijska antropologija priznaje psihološke i emocionalne dimenzije, ali upozorava da nije lako odrediti jedinstven obrazac za svaki spol.

citations.document_title: “What is Man?” (Ps 8:5). An itinerary of biblical anthropology

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the Catholic understanding of marriage because it emphasizes ongoing attention, tenderness, and mutual self-giving, and does not reduce marital closeness to satisfying a sexual need. However, the claim that women are created to be loved can sound one-sided or stereotypical if it is not clarified that husband and wife are called mutually to love and receive love.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of marital love includes both emotional closeness and bodily tenderness, but places them within mutual self-giving that respects the dignity of both; spouses are called not only to give but also to receive love as a gift. Sacred Scripture and the Church's interpretation of the marital image emphasize that Christ loves the Church self-sacrificially, while marriage is realized in mutual subjection and fidelity, not in one-sided domination. At the same time, one must avoid the assumption that all men and women feel or express love in the same way: biblical anthropology recognizes psychological and emotional dimensions, but cautions that it is not easy to determine a single pattern for each sex.
concerns_en: The formulation about women being created to be loved can be misunderstood as reducing a woman to a passive role or as claiming that men have the exclusive role of the one who loves; Catholic teaching emphasizes mutual love and mutual self-giving of spouses.

Winning over a wife must not mean an attempt to control her will or sexual readiness. The passage explicitly denies this, but it would be useful to highlight respect for her freedom and real needs even more clearly.

sections.subtitle_en: A deeper male need: to be desired, loved, and to constantly win over one's wife
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel describes the moment when he realized that his need is deeper than physical
sections.content_en:
Daniel speaks openly about his own experience. When the children were small, and his wife was tired and without the will for anything, he wondered whether it was normal that he constantly has desire, while she almost never does. That was when he realized that he, too, actually lacks the **feeling of being desired, loved, and belonging to her**. It is not just about the physical act by which a man with a great need is „satisfied”.

Daniel saw that his need goes much deeper. Although it is most often expressed through marital union, he too wants his wife to remember him, to send him a text message, and to look forward to when he returns home. Men, Daniel concludes, deceive themselves when they think they would be happier if only there were more intimacy. **Fulfillment comes from a fulfilling relationship** with the person to whom they said „yes” forever.

**Winning her over does not end with marriage**

A man cannot produce or control the will and readiness of his wife. He can, however, **continue to win her over**. Before marriage, this was natural: a little chocolate, a flower, a walk in the park, or dinner. After winning her over, many conclude that the job is done. Kruno describes this vividly with the saying that „the rabbit is no longer in the woods, the rabbit is on the spit”. Daniel agrees and adds that **women are created to be loved**. One only needs to creatively find new ways, and Kruno summarizes this as winning her over day by day.

sections.subtitle: Pornografija: ovisnost koja ne nestaje izgovorenim „da”
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel objašnjava da je pornografija ovisnost koja se prenosi u brak
sections.content:
Kruno pretpostavlja da muškarci zbog manjka bračne intimnosti bježe u pornografiju. Pita kako ona danas utječe na muškarce i čini li ih impotentnima ne samo spolno nego i emocionalno, socijalno i intelektualno.

Daniel se slaže s utjecajem, ali odmah ispravlja premisu. Pornografija, kaže, **nema veze s nedostatkom spolnosti u braku**. Većina muškaraca na nju se navikne mnogo prije nego što uopće pomisli na brak, a navika se zatim prenese i u brak. Mnogi naivno misle da je pornografija samo način nošenja sa stresom dok nemaju pristup bračnoj postelji. Zatim otkriju da i u braku jednako lako upadaju u njezine ralje.

Razlog je to što muškarac postaje **ovisan o pornografiji i zadovoljavanju požude**, a ne o spolnom činu. Tko je to radio deset ili petnaest godina prije braka, teško da će dan nakon vjenčanja reći da mu je to služilo samo da preživi. Daniel to smatra velikom zabludom. Zato je važno da se i mladi i stariji što prije uhvate u koštac s problemom i priznaju da imaju **ovisnost**. Što pornografija nije kazneno djelo ne znači da im ne treba ozbiljna pomoć.

**Impotentnost na svim razinama**

Daniel prati portale bez vjerskog ili moralnog stava o pornografiji. Na njima mladići s oduševljenjem pišu kako su nakon dva tjedna apstinencije puni ideja i uspješni na ispitima. Do tada su mislili da im pornografija čak i koristi. Sada otkrivaju svijet u kojem nisu zatupljeni ni prepušteni sami sebi i shvaćaju da bi u životu mogli nešto postići. Daniel zaključuje da je problem puno dublji od usputne teme. Upozorava i da se u vjerskim krugovima o pornografiji često govori samo moralistički, uz poruku da to ne bi trebalo. Svi znaju da je loša, ali se nitko ozbiljno ne uhvati u koštac s njom.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom jer pornografiju prikazuje kao ozbiljan problem koji može postati kompulzivan te potiče na suočavanje i traženje pomoći, a ne samo na osudu. Ipak, tvrdnje da pornografija „nema veze” s manjkom bračne spolnosti i da izaziva „impotentnost na svim razinama” izrečene su previše kategorično i nisu potkrijepljene navedenim crkvenim izvorima.
concerns: Katolički pastoralni dokument navodi različite razloge zbog kojih ljudi posežu za pornografijom, uključujući traženje utjehe zbog emocionalnih rana, te opisuje štetu za brak i odnose; zato se ne može kategorički isključiti povezanost bračnih teškoća i pornografije, iako manjak bračne spolnosti ne opravdava njezino korištenje.
Anegdotalna svjedočanstva o boljim rezultatima na ispitima nakon apstinencije ne dokazuju opći uzročni učinak, a izraz „impotentnost na svim razinama” može pretjerano uopćiti moguće posljedice.

Riječ „ovisnost” treba koristiti pažljivo: kompulzivna uporaba postoji, ali njezina težina može umanjiti osobnu moralnu odgovornost u pojedinim okolnostima, bez mijenjanja moralne naravi pornografije.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk drži da je pornografija moralno pogrešna jer spolni čin odvaja od intimnosti osoba i pretvara sudionike u predmete požude; Isus upozorava i na požudni pogled srca (Mt 5,27–28). To što nešto nije kazneno djelo ne znači da je moralno dopušteno, a borba s kompulzivnom uporabom traži i milosrđe i konkretne oblike pomoći, poput savjetovanja, duhovnog vodstva i odgovarajuće podrške.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching because it presents pornography as a serious problem that can become compulsive and encourages confronting it and seeking help, not merely condemnation. Nevertheless, the claims that pornography "has nothing to do" with a lack of marital sexuality and that it causes "impotence at all levels" are stated too categorically and are not substantiated by cited church sources.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching holds that pornography is morally wrong because it separates the sexual act from the intimacy of persons and turns participants into objects of lust; Jesus also warns of the lustful look of the heart (Mt 5:27–28). That something is not a criminal offense does not mean that it is morally permissible, and the struggle with compulsive use requires both mercy and concrete forms of help, such as counseling, spiritual direction, and appropriate support.
concerns_en: A Catholic pastoral document cites various reasons why people reach for pornography, including seeking comfort due to emotional wounds, and describes the damage to marriage and relationships; therefore, a connection between marital difficulties and pornography cannot be categorically ruled out, even though a lack of marital sexuality does not justify its use.
Anecdotal testimonies about better exam results after abstinence do not prove a general causal effect, and the expression "impotence at all levels" can overly generalize the possible consequences.

The word "addiction" should be used carefully: compulsive use exists, but its severity may diminish personal moral responsibility in certain circumstances, without changing the moral nature of pornography.

sections.subtitle_en: Pornography: an addiction that does not disappear with a spoken 'I do'
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel explains that pornography is an addiction that carries over into marriage
sections.content_en:
Kruno assumes that men escape into pornography because of a lack of marital intimacy. He asks how it affects men today and whether it makes them impotent not only sexually, but also emotionally, socially, and intellectually.

Daniel agrees with the impact, but immediately corrects the premise. Pornography, he says, **has nothing to do with the lack of sexuality in marriage**. Most men become accustomed to it long before they even think about marriage, and the habit then carries over into marriage. Many naively think that pornography is just a way of coping with stress while they do not have access to the marital bed. Then they discover that even in marriage they fall just as easily into its clutches.

The reason is that a man becomes **addicted to pornography and the satisfaction of lust**, not to the sexual act. Whoever has done that for ten or fifteen years before marriage will hardly say the day after the wedding that it only served him to survive. Daniel considers this a great delusion. That is why it is important that both young and older people grapple with the problem as soon as possible and admit that they have an **addiction**. That pornography is not a criminal offense does not mean that they do not need serious help.

**Impotence at all levels**

Daniel follows portals without a religious or moral stance on pornography. On them, young men enthusiastically write about how, after two weeks of abstinence, they are full of ideas and successful on exams. Until then, they thought pornography was even beneficial to them. Now they discover a world in which they are neither dulled nor left to themselves, and they realize that they could achieve something in life. Daniel concludes that the problem is much deeper than a passing topic. He also warns that in religious circles, pornography is often spoken of only moralistically, with the message that one shouldn't do that. Everyone knows it is bad, but no one seriously grapples with it.

sections.subtitle: Okidači, radikalni rezovi i Projekt 41: put iz ropstva
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel govori o radikalnim koracima koje muškarci moraju poduzeti da bi izašli iz ovisnosti
sections.content:
Daniel je kroz različite programe radio s muškarcima. Cilj nije bio samo da znaju kako je pornografija loša, nego da shvate **što ih do nje dovodi**: koji su im **okidači**, kad su najslabiji i u kojim joj se situacijama prepuštaju.

Ponekad su se morali dogovoriti o **radikalnim koracima**. Neki su morali ukinuti internet kod kuće ili promijeniti broj telefona kako im se ne bi javljale žene s kojima su ostvarivali ono na što ih je pornografija poticala. Tu se, kaže Daniel, vidi tko je stvarno ozbiljan. Nailazio je na otpor, primjerice na pitanje zašto bi netko mijenjao broj telefona. Daniel takvima odgovara da broj nije bitan. Tko ima dvadeset godina povijesti i nije uspio odrezati glavu toj zmiji, mora biti ekstremniji.

**Čistoća i u braku**

Kruno primjećuje da muškarci često vjeruju kako će potreba za pornografijom i samozadovoljavanjem nestati ulaskom u brak, a na kraju se prevare. Daniel dodaje da im ta **lažna nada** zapravo služi kao opravdanje. Uvjeravaju se da će prestati kad kažu „da”, kao da je to tako jednostavno. Upozorava i da se često govori samo o **predbračnoj čistoći**, kao da čistoća u braku nije potrebna. Neki se prije braka nisu upuštali u ono što ne bi trebali, a u braku nastave sa „svakakvim gadostima” s izgovorom da su se posvađali ili da nikome ne smeta ako nitko ne zna.

Daniel iznosi i osobno svjedočanstvo. Prve pornografske časopise počeo je listati s **10 ili 11 godina**, a oženio se s **24**. Takvom se sadržaju izlagao mnogo duže nego što je u prvom tjednu braka imao pristup bračnoj postelji. Zato nije realno očekivati da motivacija i stavovi preko noći nadvladaju dugogodišnje **ropstvo ovisnosti**. To treba shvatiti ozbiljno.

**Projekt 41**

Kruno navodi da danas postoji sve više programa za izlazak iz te ovisnosti. Njegova je udruga nedavno pokrenula **Projekt 41**, utemeljen na Svetom pismu i molitvi, namijenjen prije svega katoličkim muškarcima. Dolaze mu muškarci od 20 do 60 godina, u vezi ili u braku. Neki već imaju unučad, a gledaju pornografski sadržaj s djevojčicama dobi svojih unuka i ne mogu prestati. Kruno zaključuje da je to velika borba. Mogu se ponuditi svi alati, ali pomoći nema dok čovjek sam ne kaže: **„Dosta!”** Daniel se slaže.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: ispravno prikazuje pornografiju kao ozbiljan grijeh protiv čistoće i dostojanstva osobe, naglašava potrebu za čistoćom i unutar braka te potiče konkretne mjere za izbjegavanje prigoda za grijeh. Pastoralno je uvjerljiv u tome što prepoznaje dugotrajnost navike i potrebu za ozbiljnom borbom, ali izraz da pomoći nema dok čovjek sam ne kaže „Dosta!” može pretjerano sugerirati da je voljna odluka dovoljna ili da je osoba koja se još bori jednostavno nedovoljno ozbiljna.
concerns: Naglasak na osobnoj odluci važan je, ali ne bi smio zasjeniti Božju milost ni potrebu za sakramentima, odgovornošću pred drugima, savjetovanjem i stručnom pomoći, osobito kod kompulzivnog ponašanja; crkveni pastoralni pristup izričito preporučuje takvu potporu.

Radikalne praktične mjere, poput ukidanja interneta ili promjene broja, mogu biti razborita pomoć u izbjegavanju prigode za grijeh, ali ne treba ih prikazati kao jedini dokaz ozbiljnosti niti kao zamjenu za trajnu formaciju, liječenje i duhovnu pratnju.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva uči da je pornografija uvijek moralno pogrešna jer seksualnu intimnost izdvaja iz njezina bračnog i osobnog konteksta te osobe pretvara u predmete požude; to vrijedi i za supružnike. Čistoća nije samo predbračno uzdržavanje nego krepost za svaki stalež života, a u braku oblikuje vjernu, potpunu i plodnu ljubav supružnika. Istodobno, ovisnost i drugi čimbenici mogu umanjiti slobodu i osobnu odgovornost, bez promjene objektivne moralne naravi čina; put ozdravljenja uključuje ustrajnu odluku, Božju milost, ispovijed te odgovarajuću duhovnu, psihološku i zajedničku potporu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: it correctly presents pornography as a serious sin against chastity and the dignity of the person, emphasizes the need for chastity within marriage as well, and encourages concrete measures to avoid occasions of sin. It is pastorally compelling in that it recognizes the long-standing nature of the habit and the need for a serious struggle, but the expression that there is no help until a man himself says “Enough!” may excessively suggest that a volitional decision is sufficient or that a person who is still struggling is simply not serious enough.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church teaches that pornography is always morally wrong because it removes sexual intimacy from its marital and personal context and turns persons into objects of lust; this also applies to spouses. Chastity is not merely premarital abstinence, but a virtue for every state of life, and in marriage it shapes the faithful, total, and fruitful love of spouses. At the same time, addiction and other factors can diminish freedom and personal responsibility, without changing the objective moral nature of the act; the path of healing includes a persevering decision, God's grace, confession, and appropriate spiritual, psychological, and community support.
concerns_en: The emphasis on personal decision is important, but it should not overshadow God's grace nor the need for the sacraments, accountability before others, counseling, and professional help, especially in compulsive behavior; the Church's pastoral approach explicitly recommends such support.

Radical practical measures, such as canceling the internet or changing one's number, can be a prudent aid in avoiding occasions of sin, but they should not be presented as the sole proof of seriousness nor as a replacement for ongoing formation, treatment, and spiritual accompaniment.

sections.subtitle_en: Triggers, radical cuts, and Projekt 41: the path out of slavery
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel speaks about the radical steps that men must take to get out of addiction
sections.content_en:
Daniel worked with men through various programs. The goal was not only for them to know that pornography is bad, but for them to understand **what leads them to it**: what their **triggers** are, when they are at their weakest, and in which situations they surrender to it.

Sometimes they had to agree on **radical steps**. Some had to cancel the internet at home or change their phone number so that women with whom they realized what pornography incited them to would not contact them. That, Daniel says, is where one sees who is truly serious. He encountered resistance, for instance to the question of why someone would change their phone number. Daniel answers such people that the number does not matter. Whoever has twenty years of history and has not succeeded in cutting off the head of that snake must be more extreme.

**Chastity in marriage as well**

Kruno notes that men often believe that the need for pornography and masturbation will disappear upon entering marriage, but in the end they are deceived. Daniel adds that this **false hope** actually serves them as an excuse. They convince themselves that they will stop when they say “yes”, as if it were that simple. He also warns that people often speak only about **premarital chastity**, as if chastity in marriage were not necessary. Some did not engage in what they should not have before marriage, but in marriage they continue with “all kinds of foul things” with the excuse that they had an argument or that it bothers no one if no one knows.

Daniel also shares a personal testimony. He started flipping through the first pornographic magazines at **10 or 11 years old**, and he got married at **24**. He was exposed to such content much longer than he had access to the marital bed in the first week of marriage. Therefore, it is not realistic to expect that motivation and attitudes will overcome long-standing **slavery of addiction** overnight. That needs to be taken seriously.

**Projekt 41**

Kruno states that today there are more and more programs for getting out of that addiction. His association recently launched **Projekt 41**, founded on Sacred Scripture and prayer, intended primarily for Catholic men. Men from 20 to 60 years of age come to him, in a relationship or married. Some already have grandchildren, yet they watch pornographic content with girls the age of their granddaughters and cannot stop. Kruno concludes that this is a great struggle. All the tools can be offered, but there is no help until a man himself says: **“Enough!”** Daniel agrees.

sections.subtitle: Čuvali su se do braka, ali to nije vještina: razočaranja u bračnoj postelji
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel objašnjava seksualnu kompatibilnost kao vještinu koja se uči
sections.content:
Kruno otvara osjetljivu temu. Što savjetovati onima koji nisu imali spolne odnose, nisu bili izloženi pornografiji ni masturbaciji, a u braku dožive razočaranje? Neki ne znaju rade li stvari ispravno ni trebaju li se tako osjećati, pa čak izbjegavaju bračnu postelju jer im je neugodna.

Daniel priznaje da je pitanje kompleksno. U Europi i Americi sve se više govori o **„sexless marriageu”**, braku bez spolnih odnosa, koji ima različite uzroke. Smatra da treba biti pošten: tko se čuvao do braka, izgradio je karakter, vrijednosti, razmišljanje o čistoći i poštovanje prema budućoj supruzi, ali **nije razvio vještinu**.

**Seksualna kompatibilnost kao komunikacija**

Daniel ističe da je **seksualna kompatibilnost također vrsta komunikacije**. Način na koji supružnici uživaju jedno u drugome vještina je koja se uči i razvija. Oni koji su bili ovisni o pornografiji to su „naučili” kroz pornografiju, pa u bračnu sobu donose mnogo prtljage o tome što bi partneru navodno trebalo biti ugodno. Oni koji su se čuvali nisu donijeli ništa. Neki su, kao nekoć i Daniel i Kate, naivno mislili da tu nema što znati jer će se sve samo dogoditi.

Takvu sliku stvaraju i **filmovi**, u kojima je sve idealno, oboje su na kraju sretni i nitko ništa ne pita. Kruno dodaje šaljivu opasku o istodobnom orgazmu. Daniel primjećuje da nitko ne objasni ni jednostavne praktične stvari, primjerice da se nakon toga ne može odmah zaspati.

**Normalno je ne znati**

Ako je već sramotno tražiti pomoć zbog loše komunikacije, kod ove teme stigma je još veća jer je mnogo privatnija. Daniel ipak naglašava da je **potpuno normalno ne znati što se radi**. Potrebna je edukacija, primjerice dobre knjige, osobito iz **kršćanske perspektive**. Takve knjige ne prodaju seksualnost niti je uzdižu u nebesa, nego je smještaju u kontekst Bogom danog dara za uživanje i rađanje djece. Spominje i Pavlovu poslanicu **Korinćanima**, prema kojoj se supružnici ne bi trebali uzdržavati kako ih Sotona ne bi zaveo. Uz šalu dodaje da nikad nije bio u napasti posvetiti se molitvi toliko da ne bi imao vremena za svoju dragu.

Daniel i Kate nisu tražili psihološku pomoć, ali su otvoreno razgovarali sa svojim **bračnim savjetnicima**. Tom iskustvu posvećeno je jedno poglavlje knjige koju su izdali, **„Naše (ne)dovršene priče”**. U njemu opisuju kako su zapeli i shvatili da ne funkcionira pristup u kojem je muž „namiren”, a žena to „odradi”. Oboje su željeli uživati jedno u drugome i morali su otkriti kako do toga doći.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: bračnu spolnost prikazuje kao dobar dar i uzajamno izražavanje ljubavi koje supružnici mogu upoznavati kroz razgovor, a ne kao nešto što se nužno zna spontano ili treba temeljiti na pornografskim predodžbama. Tumačenje Pavla odgovara 1 Kor 7, uz važnu nijansu da se uzajamna bračna bliskost ne smije pretvarati u jednostrano pravo ili pritisak.
concerns: Izraz „bračna prava” iz 1 Kor 7 može se pogrešno shvatiti kao opravdanje za zahtijevanje spolnog odnosa bez obzira na drugoga; u samom odlomku Pavlova uputa o uzdržavanju govori o uzajamnom dogovoru i privremenom razdoblju, a naglasak na zajedničkom uživanju i razgovoru pomaže izbjeći takvo jednostrano čitanje.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje ne svodi spolnost ni na biologiju ni na tehniku: ona pripada osobnom darivanju supružnika i njihovoj vjernoj bračnoj ljubavi. Crkveni nauk zato prepoznaje da bračna nježnost može biti pozitivna vrlina i oblik uzajamne komunikacije, uz poštovanje, osjetljivost i nesebičnost. Pavao u 1 Kor 7 govori o uzajamnosti supružnika, ali izričito dopušta uzdržavanje samo uz obostrani pristanak, na određeno vrijeme i radi molitve; zato njegov tekst valja čitati oslonjeno na uzajamno poštovanje, a ne kao jednostrano nametnutu obvezu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is generally aligned with Catholic teaching: it portrays marital sexuality as a good gift and a mutual expression of love that spouses can get to know through conversation, rather than as something that is necessarily known spontaneously or should be based on pornographic notions. The interpretation of Paul corresponds to 1 Cor 7, with the important nuance that mutual marital closeness must not be turned into a unilateral right or pressure.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic understanding does not reduce sexuality either to biology or to technique: it belongs to the personal self-giving of spouses and their faithful marital love. Church teaching therefore recognizes that marital tenderness can be a positive virtue and a form of mutual communication, accompanied by respect, sensitivity, and selflessness. Paul in 1 Cor 7 speaks of the mutuality of spouses, but explicitly permits abstinence only by mutual consent, for a specified time, and for the sake of prayer; therefore, his text should be read relying on mutual respect, and not as a unilaterally imposed obligation.
concerns_en: The phrase "marital rights" from 1 Cor 7 can be misunderstood as a justification for demanding sexual intercourse regardless of the other; in the passage itself, Paul's instruction on abstinence speaks of mutual agreement and a temporary period, and the emphasis on mutual enjoyment and conversation helps avoid such a one-sided reading.

sections.subtitle_en: They saved themselves until marriage, but that is not a skill: disappointments in the marital bed
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel explains sexual compatibility as a skill that is learned
sections.content_en:
Kruno opens a sensitive topic. What advice should be given to those who have not had sexual relations, have not been exposed to pornography or masturbation, and experience disappointment in marriage? Some do not know whether they are doing things right or whether they should feel that way, and even avoid the marital bed because it is uncomfortable for them.

Daniel admits that the question is complex. In Europe and America, there is more and more talk about **"sexless marriage"**, a marriage without sexual relations, which has various causes. He believes that one should be honest: whoever saved themselves until marriage built character, values, thinking about purity, and respect toward their future wife, but **did not develop a skill**.

**Sexual compatibility as communication**

Daniel emphasizes that **sexual compatibility is also a form of communication**. The way spouses enjoy each other is a skill that is learned and developed. Those who were addicted to pornography "learned" this through pornography, so they bring a lot of baggage into the marital bedroom regarding what is supposedly pleasing to a partner. Those who saved themselves brought nothing. Some, like Daniel and Kate once did, naively thought that there was nothing to know because everything would just happen on its own.

Such a picture is also created by **movies**, where everything is ideal, both are happy in the end, and no one asks anything. Kruno adds a humorous remark about simultaneous orgasm. Daniel notices that no one explains even simple practical things, for example that one cannot immediately fall asleep after that.

**It is normal not to know**

If it is already shameful to ask for help because of poor communication, with this topic the stigma is even greater because it is much more private. Daniel nevertheless emphasizes that **it is completely normal not to know what one is doing**. Education is needed, for example good books, especially from a **Christian perspective**. Such books do not sell sexuality nor do they elevate it into the heavens, but rather place it in the context of a God-given gift for enjoyment and bearing children. He also mentions Paul's letter to the **Corinthians**, according to which spouses should not abstain so that Satan would not tempt them. With a joke, he adds that he has never been tempted to devote himself to prayer so much that he would not have time for his beloved.

Daniel and Kate did not seek psychological help, but they spoke openly with their **marriage counselors**. A chapter of the book they published, **"Naše (ne)dovršene priče"**, is dedicated to that experience. In it, they describe how they got stuck and realized that the approach where the husband is "satisfied" and the wife simply "gets it done" does not work. Both wanted to enjoy each other and had to discover how to achieve that.

sections.subtitle: Supružnika smo izabrali, dijete dobili: intimnost u godinama male djece
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel objašnjava zašto supružnici moraju namjerno ostati povezani kad dođu djeca
sections.content:
Daniel naglašava da se par mora uskladiti s razdobljem života u kojem se nalazi. Kad su djeca mala, majke su iscrpljene na svaki mogući način, pa se treba prilagoditi novoj situaciji.

Navodi i pitanje koje im je netko nedavno postavio: što ako beba spava u bračnom krevetu? Daniel ne želi roditeljima samo poručiti da beba ne smije spavati s njima. Svjestan je da je tako lakše, osobito kad majka noću doji. Kate je savjetovala da bebu na početku noći stave u njezin krevetić, a ako se u dva ujutro probudi za hranjenje, neka ostane s njima. Tako supružnici imaju barem dio večeri u kojem znaju da su sami.

To nije uvijek lako izvesti. Daniel se prisjeća da su živjeli u malom stanu sa samo spavaćom sobom i kuhinjom, pa je cijeli **kinderbet** doslovno nosio u kuhinju.

**Misao koja mijenja perspektivu**

Daniel ističe da je dijete dar i blagoslov od Boga, ali da su se supružnici **jedno drugo izabrali, a dijete su dobili**. S djetetom će roditelj uvijek ostati povezan jer mu je roditelj. Sa supružnikom **mora** ostati povezan jer ga je odabrao. Bez namjernih koraka zbližavanja dolazi do izolacije. On je umoran, ona je umorna, on je razočaran, ona nema volje, i tri tjedna kasnije pitaju se što im se dogodilo. Zato treba biti **namjerniji**.

**Prijatelji od povjerenja**

Puno im je pomoglo, a to je i Kate isticala, što ona ima nekoliko prijateljica s kojima može otvoreno razgovarati o izazovima braka. To su ljudi od povjerenja koji su spremni otvoreno reći da im nešto ne funkcionira, da ih boli ili da se ne znaju nositi s nekom situacijom. Ponekad pomaže već i to da se nekome sve ispriča. Ponekad treba potražiti konkretniju pomoć. Rješenje, prema Danielu, nikako nije zanemariti problem.

Brak bi trebao značiti da su supružnici **sjedinjeni na svakoj razini bića**: dušom, duhom i tijelom, ali i u ciljevima, interesima i obitelji koju podižu. Njihov je zadatak otkriti kako ostati zajedno.

**Posljedice pornografije na bračnu intimnost**

Daniel se na kraju ove teme vraća vlastitom iskustvu s posljedicama pornografije. Ona stvara dojam da su žene uvijek spremne i da nitko nikad nije razočaran. U stvarnosti se događa da ništa ne uspije ili da on bude gotov za tri minute, a nitko nije sretan. U početku se par samo ispriča, ali s vremenom shvati da o tome mora razgovarati i potražiti odgovarajuće rješenje.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim pogledom na brak: ističe trajnu bračnu povezanost, uzajamno darivanje, potrebu za njegovanjem odnosa i traženje pomoći, a pornografiju prikazuje kao izvor nerealnih očekivanja i štete intimnosti. Izraz da su supružnici jedno drugo izabrali, a dijete dobili može biti koristan podsjetnik na važnost braka, ali treba ga tumačiti tako da ne umanji dostojanstvo djeteta ni bračni savez kao više od svakodnevne odluke.
concerns: Suprotnost između „izabrali supružnika” i „dobili dijete” mogla bi, izvan konteksta u kojem se dijete naziva Božjim darom i blagoslovom, zvučati kao da je dijete manje važno ili tek slučajan dodatak braku.
Tvrdnju da su supružnici „sjedinjeni na svakoj razini bića” valja razumjeti kao poziv na cjelovito zajedništvo, a ne kao zahtjev da uvijek dijele iste interese, ciljeve ili osjećaje.

Primjer neuspjeha seksualnog odnosa prikazan je prvenstveno kroz razočaranje i izvedbu; korisno je naglasiti da bračna intimnost nije test uspješnosti ni obveza na odnos bez obzira na umor, zdravlje ili slobodan pristanak.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje braka obuhvaća tjelesno sjedinjenje, zajedništvo srca i života te otvorenost obiteljskom životu; dijete je plod i dar bračne ljubavi, a ne suparnik bračnom odnosu. Namjerna skrb za brak, razgovor i traženje stručne ili pastoralne pomoći odgovaraju crkvenom poticaju da supružnici brane i produbljuju bračnu vezu te potraže pratnju i praktičnu pomoć u teškoćama. Pornografija doista može narušiti povjerenje i seksualno zadovoljstvo jer osobu svodi na sredstvo užitka i stvara iskrivljena očekivanja; kršćanska čistoća, naprotiv, pomaže da bračna spolnost izražava ljubav koja se daruje.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the Catholic view of marriage: it emphasizes lasting marital connection, mutual self-giving, the need to nurture the relationship and seek help, and it portrays pornography as a source of unrealistic expectations and harm to intimacy. The expression that spouses chose each other and received the child can be a useful reminder of the importance of marriage, but it should be interpreted in a way that does not diminish the dignity of the child or the marital covenant as more than an everyday decision.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of marriage encompasses bodily union, the communion of hearts and life, and openness to family life; a child is the fruit and gift of conjugal love, not a competitor to the marital relationship. Intentional care for marriage, conversation, and seeking professional or pastoral help correspond to the Church's encouragement for spouses to defend and deepen the marital bond and to seek accompaniment and practical help in difficulties. Pornography can indeed damage trust and sexual satisfaction because it reduces the person to an instrument of pleasure and creates distorted expectations; Christian chastity, on the contrary, helps marital sexuality express a love that gives of itself.
concerns_en: The contrast between "chose a spouse" and "received a child" could, outside of the context in which a child is called God's gift and blessing, sound as though the child is less important or merely an accidental addition to the marriage.
The claim that spouses are "united on every level of being" should be understood as a call to integral communion, not as a demand that they always share the same interests, goals, or feelings.

The example of the failure of sexual intercourse is presented primarily through disappointment and performance; it is useful to emphasize that marital intimacy is not a test of success nor an obligation to intercourse regardless of fatigue, health, or free consent.

sections.subtitle_en: We chose our spouse, we received our child: intimacy in the years of young children
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel explains why spouses must intentionally stay connected when children arrive
sections.content_en:
Daniel emphasizes that a couple must align themselves with the season of life they are in. When children are small, mothers are exhausted in every possible way, so one needs to adapt to the new situation.

He also cites a question someone recently asked them: what if the baby sleeps in the marital bed? Daniel does not want to simply tell parents that the baby must not sleep with them. He is aware that it is easier that way, especially when the mother is nursing at night. Kate advised putting the baby in its crib at the beginning of the night, and if it wakes up at two in the morning to feed, let it stay with them. That way, the spouses have at least part of the evening in which they know they are alone.

That is not always easy to accomplish. Daniel recalls that they lived in a small apartment with only a bedroom and a kitchen, so he literally carried the entire **crib** into the kitchen.

**A thought that changes perspective**

Daniel points out that a child is a gift and a blessing from God, but that the spouses **chose each other, and received the child**. A parent will always remain connected to a child because they are its parent. With a spouse, one **must** remain connected because one chose them. Without intentional steps toward growing closer, isolation occurs. He is tired, she is tired, he is disappointed, she has no desire, and three weeks later they wonder what happened to them. That is why one needs to be **more intentional**.

**Trusted friends**

It helped them a lot, and Kate emphasized this as well, that she has several female friends with whom she can openly discuss the challenges of marriage. These are trusted people who are ready to say openly that something is not working for them, that they are hurting, or that they do not know how to handle a situation. Sometimes it already helps just to tell everything to someone. Sometimes one needs to seek more concrete help. The solution, according to Daniel, is by no means to ignore the problem.

Marriage should mean that the spouses are **united on every level of being**: in soul, spirit, and body, but also in goals, interests, and the family they are raising. Their task is to discover how to stay together.

**The consequences of pornography on marital intimacy**

At the end of this topic, Daniel returns to his own experience with the consequences of pornography. It creates the impression that women are always ready and that no one is ever disappointed. In reality, what happens is that nothing works out or that he is done in three minutes, and no one is happy. In the beginning, the couple just makes an excuse, but over time they realize they must talk about it and look for an appropriate solution.

sections.subtitle: Nije problem koliko novca imate, nego kako ga trošite
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel Wurzberg objašnjava da financijski problemi u braku ne ovise o visini primanja
sections.content:
Nakon razgovora o spolnosti, voditelj **Kruno** prelazi na temu koja, kako kaže, u braku najčešće dolazi do izražaja odmah uz intimnost: **financije**. Primjećuje da muškarce možda najviše boli kada ih se udari po novčaniku, jednako kao kada ih se udari po intimnosti. Zato pita gosta kakva su iskustva iz bračnog savjetovanja.

**Daniel Wurzberg** kao prvi problem navodi lažnu uvjerenost parova da su na tom području kompatibilni. Iskustvo udruge Fokus pokazuje nešto što mnoge iznenadi: problem gotovo nikad nije u tome koliko novca par ima. *„Puno ili malo novaca, to je zapravo svejedno, uvijek je izazov kako ih trošite“*, ističe Daniel.

Objašnjava da se oba supružnika obično znaju prilagoditi oskudici. Kad par ima samo jednu plaću, pola plaće ili su oboje ostali bez posla, znaju se „stisnuti“. Problem nastaje kada su se oboje odrekli nečega, a jedan od njih sebi ipak kupi što poželi, dok drugi to nije mogao. Daniel to slikovito opisuje: oboje su bili spremni na žrtvu, a onda je jedan otišao na dvije kave, iako se kava mogla piti i kod kuće.

### Anegdota o 20.000 kuna

Kao drugu stranu iste priče Daniel navodi susret s jednim mladićem. Bilo je to još u vrijeme kuna, a mladić mu se požalio: *„Gle, ja imam 20.000 kn mjesečno, ja si ni majicu ne mogu priuštit.“* Daniel se tada zapitao kako je to moguće, jer je on sam imao pet puta manja primanja i troje djece. Zaključak je jasan: **nije problem imati novac, nego kako se njime upravlja.**

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim shvaćanjem braka jer ističe uzajamnu odgovornost, obzirnost i spremnost na svakodnevnu žrtvu, a ne samo visinu prihoda. Njegov naglasak na dogovoru i pravednosti u trošenju odgovara biblijskom pozivu supružnicima da njeguju nesebičnu ljubav i zajednički rješavaju razlike.
concerns: Tvrdnju da problem gotovo nikad nije u visini prihoda valja shvatiti kao iskustvo savjetovanja, a ne kao univerzalno pravilo: materijalna oskudica može biti ozbiljan obiteljski teret.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanski brak uključuje svakodnevni put svetosti, u kojemu se ljubav očituje i kroz radosti i kroz žrtve te odgovornost prema supružniku i djeci. Zato financijski dogovor nije samo tehničko pitanje budžeta: supružnici su pozvani uzajamno uvažavati potrebe i okolnosti drugoga te zajedno donositi odgovorne odluke.

Its emphasis on agreement and justice in spending corresponds to the biblical call to spouses to cultivate selfless love and resolve differences together.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christian marriage includes a daily path of holiness, in which love is manifested both through joys and through sacrifices as well as responsibility toward one's spouse and children. sections.subtitle_en: The problem is not how much money you have, but how you spend it
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel Wurzberg explains that financial problems in marriage do not depend on the level of income
sections.content_en:
After the conversation about sexuality, the host **Kruno** moves on to a topic that, as he says, most often comes to the fore in marriage right alongside intimacy: **finances**. He notes that men are perhaps hurt the most when they are hit in the wallet, just as when they are hit in intimacy. That is why he asks the guest what the experiences from marriage counseling are.

**Daniel Wurzberg** cites as the first problem couples' false conviction that they are compatible in that area. The experience of the association Fokus shows something that surprises many: the problem is almost never in how much money a couple has. *“A lot or a little money, it is actually all the same, the challenge is always how you spend it,”* Daniel emphasizes.

He explains that both spouses usually know how to adapt to scarcity. When a couple has only one salary, half a salary, or both have lost their jobs, they know how to “tighten up.” The problem arises when both have given up something, and one of them still buys whatever they want for themselves, while the other could not. Daniel vividly describes it: both were ready for sacrifice, and then one went for two coffees, even though coffee could have been drunk at home.

### Anecdote about 20,000 Kuna

As the other side of the same story, Daniel mentions an encounter with a young man. It was back in the time of kunas, and the young man complained to him: *“Look, I have 20,000 kn a month, I can't even afford a T-shirt.”* Daniel then wondered how that was possible, because he himself had five times lower income and three children. The conclusion is clear: **the problem is not having money, but how it is managed.**

sections.subtitle: Lekcija o novcu tek nakon medenog mjeseca
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o vrijednostima iz roditeljskog doma i o tome zašto se lekcija o financijama ostavlja za kraj tečaja
sections.content:
Prema Danielu, veliku ulogu u odnosu prema novcu imaju **vrijednosti koje supružnici donose iz svojih obitelji**. Važno je kako su njihovi roditelji upravljali financijama, tko je za to bio odgovoran te jesu li se stalno mučili da spoje kraj s krajem ili su novcem upravljali mudro. Mnogo toga ovisi o tome kakav se par nađe, no o financijama se u svakom slučaju mora razgovarati.

Daniel to smatra jednom od važnijih lekcija. Zato u udruzi u posljednje vrijeme na zaručničkim tečajevima **lekciju o financijama ostavljaju za razdoblje nakon medenog mjeseca**. Objašnjava razlog: na medenom mjesecu mladenci se obično dobro počaste, s osjećajem da si mogu priuštiti što god žele. Onda ih udari svakodnevica u kojoj idu na posao i žive od plaće do plaće.

Tek se tada, kaže Daniel, jasnije vidi s kakvim vrijednostima supružnici pristupaju vođenju kućnog budžeta. Kruno dodaje da se do tada „skupi materijala“, a Daniel se slaže.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim pogledom na brak jer ističe važnost razgovora, zajedničke odgovornosti i svakodnevnog obiteljskog života, bez tvrdnji koje bi proturječile nauku ili Svetom pismu. Financije prikazuje kao praktično područje bračnog zajedništva, premda ih ne povezuje izričito s kršćanskim upravljanjem dobrima i služenjem obitelji.
concerns: Odgađanje posebne lekcije o financijama do nakon medenog mjeseca može biti pastoralno nepraktično ako se time odgađa i važan razgovor o prihodima, troškovima i očekivanjima; odlomak, međutim, ne kaže da se o tome prije vjenčanja uopće ne razgovara.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveno predvjenčano pripravljanje treba biti primjereno, a bračna zajednica gradi se u konkretnim svakodnevnim područjima poput doma i rada, ne samo u posebnim trenucima. Zato je razgovor o obiteljskim navikama i kućnom budžetu smislen dio priprave, dok bi praktične teme bilo dobro povezati s uzajamnim poštovanjem, odgovornošću i zajedničkim razlučivanjem supružnika.
