magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mostly aligned with the Catholic view of marriage because it emphasizes the importance of conversation, shared responsibility, and everyday family life, without claims that would contradict teaching or Sacred Scripture. It portrays finances as a practical area of marital communion, although it does not explicitly connect them with Christian stewardship of goods and service to the family.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church's pre-marriage preparation should be adequate, and the marital communion is built in concrete everyday areas such as home and work, not only in special moments. Therefore, conversation about family habits and the household budget is a meaningful part of preparation, while it would be good to connect practical topics with mutual respect, responsibility, and the spouses' shared discernment.
concerns_en: Postponing a specific lesson on finances until after the honeymoon can be pastorally impractical if this also postpones an important conversation about income, expenses, and expectations; the passage, however, does not say that this is not discussed at all before the wedding.

sections.subtitle_en: A lesson about money only after the honeymoon
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about values from the parental home and about why the lesson on finances is left for the end of the course
sections.content_en:
According to Daniel, a major role in the attitude toward money is played by **the values that spouses bring from their families**. It is important how their parents managed finances, who was responsible for that, and whether they constantly struggled to make ends meet or managed money wisely. A lot depends on what kind of couple comes together, but finances must be discussed in any case.

Daniel considers this one of the more important lessons. That is why in the association recently, in pre-Cana courses, **they leave the lesson on finances for the period after the honeymoon**. He explains the reason: on the honeymoon, newlyweds usually treat themselves well, with the feeling that they can afford whatever they want. Then everyday life hits them, in which they go to work and live from paycheck to paycheck.

Only then, Daniel says, can it be seen more clearly with what values the spouses approach managing the household budget. Kruno adds that by then "material accumulates," and Daniel agrees.

sections.subtitle: Kad novac postane oruđe manipulacije
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel Wurzberg opisuje slučaj para u kojem je posuđeni novac narušio povjerenje
sections.content:
Daniel naglašava da razočaranja i prve svađe oko novca nisu nepremostive, ali da se **povjerenje mora graditi**. Kao primjer navodi par u kojem je muž posudio novac od roditelja svoje supruge. Novac nije iskoristio za ono što je obećao, nego je negdje nestao. Daniel ne zna je li ga prokockao ili je bilo nešto slično.

Potrošeni novac pritom nije bio glavni problem. Muž je taj iznos mogao zaraditi i vratiti kroz nekoliko mjeseci. Glavni problem bilo je **narušeno povjerenje**. Rečenica više nije glasila *„Dužan si mojim roditeljima“*, nego *„Ne mogu ti vjerovati“*. Daniel ističe razliku: da se mužu razbio auto pa je par završio u minusu, to bi bila jedna priča. Ovdje je, međutim, riječ o iskorištenom povjerenju i pitanju kako dalje.

Njegov zaključak je ozbiljan. Ako par primijeti da novcem pokušava **manipulirati jedno drugim**, da potajno nešto kupuje ili skriva, tada ima mnogo dublji problem kojim se mora pozabaviti.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim shvaćanjem braka jer razlikuje nepredviđenu financijsku teškoću od svjesnog prikrivanja ili zloupotrebe povjerenja, te takvo ponašanje ne umanjuje na puki novčani gubitak. Dobro je i što ne tvrdi da zna što se dogodilo s novcem, nego zaključak veže uz obrazac manipulacije ili skrivanja.
magisterium.enrichment: U braku, koji je zajedništvo života, istinoljubivost i uzajamna odgovornost za zajednička dobra podupiru povjerenje; biblijska slika supružnika kao „jednoga tijela” daje tom zajedništvu dublji smisao (Post 2,24). Crkveni sudski slučaj o skrivenom kockanju pokazuje da tajne financijske navike mogu ozbiljno utjecati na povjerenje i bračnu odluku, ali i da se okolnosti moraju pomno utvrditi, a ne zaključivati bez dokaza. Razlikovanje financijskog gubitka zbog nezgode od namjerne obmane zato je moralno važno; ozbiljan problem traži iskren razgovor i nastojanje oko odgovornosti i obnove povjerenja.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the Catholic understanding of marriage because it distinguishes unforeseen financial hardship from deliberate concealment or abuse of trust, and does not reduce such behavior to a mere monetary loss. It is also good that it does not claim to know what happened to the money, but connects the conclusion to a pattern of manipulation or hiding.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In marriage, which is a communion of life, truthfulness and mutual responsibility for common goods support trust; the biblical image of the spouses as "one body" gives that communion a deeper meaning (Gen 2:24). An ecclesiastical court case regarding hidden gambling shows that secret financial habits can seriously affect trust and the marital decision, but also that circumstances must be carefully determined, rather than concluded without evidence. Distinguishing a financial loss due to an accident from intentional deception is therefore morally important; a serious problem requires an honest conversation and an effort toward responsibility and the renewal of trust.

sections.subtitle_en: When Money Becomes a Tool of Manipulation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel Wurzberg describes the case of a couple in which borrowed money damaged trust
sections.content_en:
Daniel emphasizes that disappointments and first arguments about money are not insurmountable, but that **trust must be built**. As an example, he cites a couple in which the husband borrowed money from his wife's parents. He did not use the money for what he had promised, but rather it disappeared somewhere. Daniel does not know whether he gambled it away or whether it was something similar.

The spent money, at that, was not the main problem. The husband could have earned and returned that amount over a few months. The main problem was **damaged trust**. The sentence was no longer *"You owe my parents"*, but *"I cannot trust you"*. Daniel points out the difference: if the husband's car had broken down so the couple ended up in the red, that would be one story. Here, however, it is a matter of exploited trust and the question of how to move forward.

His conclusion is serious. If a couple notices that they are trying to **manipulate each other** with money, that someone is secretly buying something or hiding it, then they have a much deeper problem that must be dealt with.

sections.subtitle: „Naše (ne)dovršene priče“: razvodi koji se nisu dogodili
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj predstavlja knjigu „Naše nedovršene priče – Razvodi koji se nisu dogodili“
sections.content:
Kruno zatim predstavlja knjigu **„Naše nedovršene priče – Razvodi koji se nisu dogodili“**. Naziva je sjajnom knjigom punom svjedočanstava i plodom rada udruge. Ističe da je poticajno čitati priče parova koji su došli gotovo do ruba, a ipak su uspjeli nadići krizu. Svaki čitatelj, smatra, može se prepoznati u nekom od svjedočanstava. Zato pita gosta koja je priča njemu osobno progovorila.

Daniel odgovara da na njega nisu najveći dojam ostavile same priče, nego **proces kroz koji su autori prošli dok su ih pisali**. Pojašnjava i naslov. Knjiga se ne zove „Razvodi koji se nisu dogodili“ zato što su svi parovi nužno bili pred razvodom. Neke priče govore o svakodnevnom trenju, na primjer o paru u kojem je on ekstrovert, a ona introvert, pa se oko toga stalno natežu. To nije razlog za razvod, ali je stalan izvor napetosti.

Zanimljivo je da je Daniel ranije u razgovoru otkrio kako jedno poglavlje knjige govori i o njegovu braku s Kate. U njemu opisuju razdoblje u kojem su na području intime „zapeli“ i potražili pomoć bračnih savjetnika.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim pogledom na brak: svakodnevne napetosti i krize ne prikazuje kao automatski razlog za razvod, a traženje pomoći predstavlja kao konstruktivan odgovor. Ne iznosi izričitu teološku tvrdnju o nerazrješivosti ženidbene veze, ali joj ništa u opisu ne proturječi.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk prepoznaje da krize, nesporazumi i razdoblja napetosti mogu biti dio bračnog života, a uz pomoć, pomirenje i milost mogu postati prilika za sazrijevanje odnosa. Crkva zato potiče pratnju parova u krizi te, kada je potrebno, stručnu pomoć, uz duhovnu skrb i oslanjanje na Krista.

It does not state an explicit theological claim about the indissolubility of the marital bond, but nothing in the description contradicts it.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching recognizes that crises, misunderstandings, and periods of tension can be part of married life, and with help, reconciliation, and grace, they can become an opportunity for the relationship to mature. The Church therefore encourages the accompaniment of couples in crisis and, when necessary, professional help, alongside spiritual care and reliance on Christ.

sections.subtitle_en: "Our (Un)finished Stories": Divorces That Did Not Happen
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host presents the book "Our Unfinished Stories – Divorces That Did Not Happen"
sections.content_en:
Kruno then presents the book **"Our Unfinished Stories – Divorces That Did Not Happen"**. He calls it a great book full of testimonies and the fruit of the association's work. He points out that it is encouraging to read the stories of couples who came almost to the brink, yet managed to overcome the crisis. Every reader, he believes, can recognize themselves in one of the testimonies. Therefore, he asks the guest which story spoke to him personally.

Daniel answers that it was not the stories themselves that left the greatest impression on him, but **the process through which the authors went while writing them**. He also clarifies the title. The book is not called "Divorces That Did Not Happen" because all the couples were necessarily facing divorce. Some stories speak of everyday friction, for example about a couple in which he is an extrovert and she is an introvert, so they constantly clash over it. That is not a reason for divorce, but it is a constant source of tension.

It is interesting that Daniel revealed earlier in the conversation that one chapter of the book also speaks about his marriage with Kate. In it, they describe a period in which they "got stuck" in the area of intimacy and sought the help of marriage counselors.

sections.subtitle: Pisanje kao terapija: priča o tri spontana pobačaja
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel Wurzberg prepričava svjedočanstvo para koji je prošao kroz tri spontana pobačaja
sections.content:
Urednici knjige postavili su autorima dva ključna uvjeta:

- **Oba supružnika moraju napisati svoju perspektivu.** Nije bilo dovoljno da, primjerice, samo žena hrabro opiše kako je bilo.
- **Pišu iz perspektive razdoblja kroz koje su prolazili**, a ne samo iz današnje, smirenije pozicije.

Rezultat je iznenadio i same urednike. Neki su parovi priznali da im je pisanje bilo **kao terapija**. Jedna supruga rekla je da zapravo nikad nije čula kako se njezin muž nosio s onim kroz što su prošli zajedno.

Daniel posebno izdvaja priču para koji je doživio **tri spontana pobačaja**. Objašnjava da se spontani pobačaj može dogoditi u svakoj trudnoći. Nakon prvoga par se tješi da će ih Bog iscijeliti i da će pokušati ponovno. Nakon trećega, međutim, javljaju se teška pitanja: je li kriv on, je li kriva ona, što ne valja. Muž je u knjizi napisao da prvi pobačaj nije doživio teško jer su znali da se može dogoditi. No kada je nakon trećega morao ići u bolnicu, to je doživio sasvim drugačije. Supruga je tek tada čula kako se on s tim nosio.

Daniel zaključuje da je prilika da ispričaju svoju priču parovima dala više od platforme. Omogućila im je da **procesuiraju bol** kroz koju su prošli. Neki od njih u braku su već po 30 godina, a tek su sada otkrili dio svog odnosa koji nikad nisu izrekli riječima. Bog ih je vjerno nosio kroz to razdoblje, ali tek su sada mogli reći: *„Nisam znala da si se tako osjećao, da te to toliko boljelo.“* Za Daniela je to najdublji dojam: da su se supružnici vidjeli i čuli na novi način.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim pogledom jer priznaje gubitak djeteta, dopušta da supružnici različito proživljavaju žalost i naglašava slušanje, zajedništvo i vjerno Božje praćenje. Ne prikazuje spontani pobačaj kao kaznu, krivnju jednog od supružnika ili dokaz nedostatka vjere.
concerns: Izraz da će ih Bog „iscijeliti” može biti dvosmislen ako bi se shvatio kao obećanje da će bol brzo nestati ili da će uslijediti nova trudnoća; u odlomku je, međutim, prikazan kao nada i utjeha para, a ne kao jamstvo takva ishoda.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička vjera ne zahtijeva da roditelji prikrivaju žalost: Amoris laetitia podsjeća da je i Isus plakao te izričito priznaje tjeskobu roditelja koji su izgubili dijete (Iv 11,33.35). Crkvena molitva za roditelje nakon gubitka djeteta moli za utjehu u Božjoj ljubavi i povjerava dijete Božjem milosrđu, dok pastoralno praćenje žalovanja traži strpljenje i uvažavanje pitanja koja se u tom procesu javljaju.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the Catholic perspective because it acknowledges the loss of a child, allows spouses to experience grief differently, and emphasizes listening, communion, and God's faithful accompaniment. It does not present miscarriage as a punishment, the fault of one of the spouses, or proof of a lack of faith.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic faith does not require parents to conceal grief: Amoris laetitia recalls that Jesus also wept and explicitly acknowledges the anguish of parents who have lost a child (Jn 11:33, 35). The Church's prayer for parents after the loss of a child prays for comfort in God's love and entrusts the child to God's mercy, while pastoral accompaniment of mourning calls for patience and respect for the questions that arise in that process.
concerns_en: The expression that God will “heal” them can be ambiguous if understood as a promise that the pain will quickly disappear or that a new pregnancy will follow; in the passage, however, it is presented as the couple's hope and consolation, not as a guarantee of such an outcome.

sections.subtitle_en: Writing as therapy: a story of three miscarriages
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel Wurzberg recounts the testimony of a couple who went through three miscarriages
sections.content_en:
The editors of the book set two key conditions for the authors:

- **Both spouses must write their perspective.** It was not enough for, for example, only the wife to courageously describe how it was.
- **They write from the perspective of the period they were going through**, and not just from today's, calmer position.

The result surprised even the editors themselves. Some couples admitted that writing was **like therapy** for them. One wife said that she had actually never heard how her husband coped with what they went through together.

Daniel especially highlights the story of a couple who experienced **three miscarriages**. He explains that a miscarriage can happen in any pregnancy. After the first one, the couple consoles themselves that God will heal them and that they will try again. After the third one, however, difficult questions arise: is it his fault, is it her fault, what is wrong. The husband wrote in the book that he did not experience the first miscarriage as difficult because they knew it could happen. But when he had to go to the hospital after the third one, he experienced it completely differently. Only then did the wife hear how he coped with it.

Daniel concludes that the opportunity to tell their story gave the couples more than a platform. It enabled them to **process the pain** they went through. Some of them have been married for as long as 30 years, and only now have they discovered a part of their relationship that they had never put into words. God faithfully carried them through that period, but only now could they say: *“I didn't know that you felt that way, that it hurt you so much.”* For Daniel, that is the deepest impression: that the spouses saw and heard each other in a new way.

sections.subtitle: Male grupe i brak koji živi misijski
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o pitanjima za promišljanje i važnosti malih grupa za bračne parove
sections.content:
Pisanje nije pomoglo samo autorima, nego obogaćuje i čitatelje. Daniel priznaje da se ne može svatko poistovjetiti sa svakom pričom. Jedna od njih, primjerice, govori o **bankrotu**. Ipak, svi znaju kako je imati ili nemati novac i boriti se da se plate računi, pa se i s takvom pričom čitatelj može povezati.

Svaka priča završava **s nekoliko pitanja za promišljanje**. Daniel ističe da je upravo to cijela ideja knjige. Ona nije samo zbirka svjedočanstava, nego bi trebala potaknuti razgovor, posebno u maloj grupi. U Fokusu su, kaže, *„strastveno uvjereni“* da je **mala grupa plodno tlo za svaki brak**. U njoj parovi uče na primjeru drugih i prije svega otkrivaju da nisu sami i da nisu ludi.

Daniel nabraja s čime se parovi bore:

- s problemima u bračnoj postelji,
- s financijama,
- s odgojem djece,
- s nemogućnošću da imaju djecu, što je tema jedne od priča u knjizi.

Kad par otkrije krug ljudi s kojima može rasti i dijeliti vrijednosti, lakše ide dalje. Daniel se nada da Bog takve priče može iskoristiti i da ohrabri ljude koje autori nikad neće sresti uživo. Takvi čitatelji možda će se zapitati kako ono kroz što su sami prošli može biti Bogu na slavu.

Krajnji je cilj potaknuti parove da otkriju kako se **brak može živjeti na misijski način**. Brak ne postoji samo radi dvoje supružnika, nego i radi društva u kojem žive. Može biti svjedočanstvo djeci, roditeljima, rodbini, a zatim i mnogo širem krugu ljudi.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je u bitnome usklađen s katoličkim naukom: prikazuje brak kao poziv koji se živi uz potporu zajednice i kao svjedočanstvo koje nadilazi dobrobit samih supružnika. Neplodnost i druge teškoće spominju se bez tvrdnje da umanjuju vrijednost braka ili da se mogu lako riješiti.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje braka povezuje zajedništvo supružnika s poslanjem u obitelji i društvu; kršćanski supružnici svjedoče ljubavlju i mogu drugima prenositi vjeru, pa je govor o „misijskom braku” primjeren ako ne zasjeni dostojanstvo i dobro samih supružnika. Mala grupa može biti korisna potpora, ali ne zamjenjuje sakramentalnu milost, župnu zajednicu ni stručno pastoralno vodstvo kada su teškoće ozbiljne. Brak bez djece ne gubi svoju bitnu vrijednost, što pruža važan kontekst za spomen neplodnosti.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is substantially aligned with Catholic teaching: it presents marriage as a vocation lived with the support of the community and as a witness that transcends the well-being of the spouses themselves. Infertility and other difficulties are mentioned without claiming that they diminish the value of marriage or that they can be easily resolved.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of marriage connects the communion of spouses with a mission in the family and society; Christian spouses bear witness through love and can transmit the faith to others, so speaking of a “missional marriage” is appropriate if it does not overshadow the dignity and good of the spouses themselves. A small group can be a useful support, but it does not replace sacramental grace, the parish community, or professional pastoral guidance when difficulties are serious. A childless marriage does not lose its essential value, which provides an important context for the mention of infertility.

sections.subtitle_en: Small groups and a marriage that lives missionally
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about reflection questions and the importance of small groups for married couples
sections.content_en:
Writing did not help only the authors, but it also enriches readers. Daniel admits that not everyone can identify with every story. One of them, for example, speaks about **bankruptcy**. Still, everyone knows what it is like to have or not have money and to struggle to pay the bills, so a reader can connect even with such a story.

Each story ends **with several questions for reflection**. Daniel emphasizes that this is precisely the whole idea of the book. It is not merely a collection of testimonies, but should prompt conversation, especially in a small group. In Fokus, he says, they are *“passionately convinced”* that **a small group is fertile ground for every marriage**. In it, couples learn from the example of others and, above all, discover that they are not alone and that they are not crazy.

Daniel lists what couples struggle with:

- with problems in the marital bed,
- with finances,
- with raising children,
- with the inability to have children, which is the theme of one of the stories in the book.

When a couple discovers a circle of people with whom they can grow and share values, it is easier to move forward. Daniel hopes that God can use such stories and encourage people whom the authors will never meet in person. Such readers may wonder how what they themselves have gone through can be for God's glory.

The ultimate goal is to encourage couples to discover how **marriage can be lived in a missional way**. Marriage does not exist only for the sake of the two spouses, but also for the sake of the society in which they live. It can be a witness to children, parents, relatives, and then to a much broader circle of people.

sections.subtitle: Od Tjedna braka do serijala „Budi odvažan“
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel Wurzberg predstavlja program „Budi odvažan“, video serijal od deset lekcija za muškarce
sections.content:
Kruno priznaje da mu je epizoda proletjela i da bi se o knjizi moglo govoriti mnogo duže. Prije kraja izdvaja još neke projekte udruge Fokus:

- **Nacionalni tjedan braka**, koji se održava tjedan dana prije Valentinova,
- **Vikende za pamćenje**, okupljanja na određenoj lokaciji namijenjena samo bračnim parovima, najčešće bez djece, što voditelj smatra velikim plusom.

Zatim pita kako udruga pristupa muškarcima i postoji li program posvećen samo njima.

Daniel potvrđuje da postoji. Riječ je o programu **„Budi odvažan“**, video serijalu od **deset lekcija** koji obrađuje teme s kojima se bori većina muškaraca. Među njima su:

- pitanje vlastitog identiteta,
- različite ovisnosti,
- pornografija, o kojoj se u razgovoru već govorilo.

Serijal želi pokazati muškarcu da može učiniti mnogo više za zajednicu u kojoj živi. To uključuje odgovornost onoga koji se brine za svoj dom, dobro ljubljenje vlastite supruge i uključivanje u živote drugih muškaraca. Daniel opisuje i dvostruku ulogu mentorstva. S jedne strane muškarac treba **imati mentora**, nekoga starijeg i zrelijeg tko će govoriti u njegov život. S druge strane i sam treba **postati mentor** mlađima i otkriti da može nešto dati ako za to odvoji vrijeme i bude namjeran.

magisterium.assessment: Opis je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: odgovornost za obitelj, vjernost supruzi, borba protiv pornografije i ovisnosti te uzajamno mentorstvo mogu podupirati kršćanski poziv na ljubav, služenje i rast u kreposti. Sam odlomak ne iznosi pojedinosti lekcija, pa se njihova cjelovita teološka usklađenost ne može procijeniti.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska odgovornost muža nije nadmoć nad suprugom, nego velikodušno služenje i poštovanje njezina jednakog dostojanstva; sveti Pavao poziva muževe da ljube svoje žene kao što je Krist ljubio Crkvu (Ef 5,25), a Crkva očinsku ulogu povezuje s brigom za dobro obitelji i odgoj djece. Pornografija šteti sposobnosti za samodarivanje i uzajamno poštovanje, a ovisnost može otežati slobodu, zbog čega su pomoć, odgovornost i nada u ozdravljenje važni. Mentorstvo može biti konkretan oblik potpore u življenju poziva na ljubav i odgovorno služenje, ali valja ga provoditi uz poštovanje dostojanstva i slobode svake osobe.

The passage itself does not present the details of the lessons, so their complete theological alignment cannot be assessed.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Christian responsibility of a husband is not dominance over his wife, but generous service and respect for her equal dignity; Saint Paul calls husbands to love their wives as Christ loved the Church (Eph 5:25), and the Church connects the paternal role with caring for the good of the family and the upbringing of children. Pornography harms the capacity for self-giving and mutual respect, and addiction can impair freedom, which is why help, accountability, and hope for healing are important. Mentorship can be a concrete form of support in living the call to love and responsible service, but it must be carried out while respecting the dignity and freedom of every person.

sections.subtitle_en: From Marriage Week to the series "Budi odvažan"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel Wurzberg presents the program "Budi odvažan", a video series of ten lessons for men
sections.content_en:
Kruno admits that the episode flew by for him and that much more could be said about the book. Before concluding, he highlights a few more projects of the association Fokus:

- **Nacionalni tjedan braka**, which takes place a week before Valentine's Day,
- **Vikendi za pamćenje**, gatherings at a specific location intended only for married couples, most often without children, which the host considers a big plus.

He then asks how the association approaches men and whether there is a program dedicated solely to them.

Daniel confirms that there is. It is the program **"Budi odvažan"**, a video series of **ten lessons** addressing topics that most men struggle with. Among them are:

- the question of one's own identity,
- various addictions,
- pornography, which had already been discussed in the conversation.

The series aims to show a man that he can do much more for the community in which he lives. This includes the responsibility of one who cares for his home, loving his own wife well, and being involved in the lives of other men. Daniel also describes the twofold role of mentorship. On the one hand, a man needs to **have a mentor**, someone older and more mature who will speak into his life. On the other hand, he himself needs to **become a mentor** to younger men and discover that he can give something if he sets aside time for it and is intentional.

sections.subtitle: Kobasice na vatri i vjera koja ne staje nedjeljom
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje „Budi odvažan“ vikend u Gorskom kotaru
sections.content:
Program se provodi svaka dva tjedna, pa deset susreta traje nekoliko mjeseci. Daniel je, međutim, svjestan da muškarci neće samo sjediti oko stola i razgovarati o onome što je dobro za njihov život. Zato se jednom godišnje održava **„Budi odvažan“ vikend u Gorskom kotaru**. Tamo sudionici peku kobasice na vatri i planinare, ali i promišljaju kako izgleda vjera u životu pobožnog muškarca.

Pitanja koja si postavljaju vrlo su konkretna: kako vjera izgleda na poslu, kako u obitelji, a kako u životu studenta i njegovu svjedočanstvu ondje gdje se nalazi. Cilj je, ističe Daniel, da se vjera ne svede na nešto što se događa nedjeljom, dok muškarac od ponedjeljka do subote živi kako zna, a onda je opet malo pobožan.

Vikend u šumi oduševljava muškarce. Upoznaju sebe i druge, a posebno oni koji dolaze iz grada otkrivaju da ipak postoje ljudi s kojima mogu podijeliti takve stvari i koji ih razumiju.

Daniel ipak naglašava da jedan vikend neće nikome promijeniti cijelu godinu ako nakon toga ne ulaže u područja koja je otkrio. Navodi primjere: netko se cijeli život smatra vjernikom, a shvati da nikad sam nije pročitao Bibliju. Drugi dobro zarađuje za obitelj, ali uvidi da kod kuće ima djecu koja ga trebaju, a on za njih nema vremena upravo zato što radi. Takav bi, sugerira Daniel, mogao sljedeći put na vikend povesti sina ili mu se na neki drugi način približiti.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je snažno usklađen s katoličkim razumijevanjem vjere kao stvarnosti koja prožima svakodnevni život, a ne samo nedjeljno bogoslužje, te s poticajem da se Sveto pismo upoznaje i čita. Također primjereno naglašava da se vjera očituje u konkretnim odnosima i odgovornostima, uključujući prisutnost oca u životu djece.
magisterium.enrichment: Benedikt XVI. ističe da se susret sa Svetim pismom treba produbljivati i usvajati u životu vjernika te da čitanje Biblije produbljuje osobni odnos s Isusom; zato je poticaj da netko tko se smatra vjernikom počne sam čitati Bibliju u skladu s katoličkom duhovnošću. Katolički pogled ne suprotstavlja vjeru svakodnevnim obvezama: vjera treba oblikovati običan život, rad i odnose, dok pružanje materijalne skrbi obitelji ne opravdava zanemarivanje djece i njihove potrebe za očevom prisutnošću.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is strongly aligned with the Catholic understanding of faith as a reality that permeates everyday life, and not only Sunday worship, and with the encouragement to know and read Sacred Scripture. It also appropriately emphasizes that faith is manifested in concrete relationships and responsibilities, including the presence of the father in the life of his children.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Benedict XVI emphasizes that the encounter with Sacred Scripture should be deepened and assimilated into the life of the believer and that reading the Bible deepens a personal relationship with Jesus; therefore, the encouragement for someone who considers himself a believer to begin reading the Bible on his own is in accordance with Catholic spirituality. The Catholic view does not oppose faith to everyday obligations: faith should shape ordinary life, work, and relationships, while providing material care for the family does not justify neglecting children and their need for a father's presence.

sections.subtitle_en: Sausages over the fire and faith that does not stop on Sunday
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes the "Budi odvažan" weekend in Gorski kotar
sections.content_en:
The program is carried out every two weeks, so ten meetings last several months. Daniel is, however, aware that men will not just sit around a table and talk about what is good for their lives. That is why the **"Budi odvažan" weekend in Gorski kotar** is held once a year. There, participants roast sausages over the fire and hike, but also reflect on what faith looks like in the life of a devout man.

The questions they ask themselves are very concrete: what faith looks like at work, what it looks like in the family, and what it looks like in the life of a student and his testimony where he is. The goal, Daniel points out, is for faith not to be reduced to something that happens on Sunday, while from Monday to Saturday a man lives as best he can, and then is a little devout again.

The weekend in the forest delights the men. They get to know themselves and others, and especially those coming from the city discover that there are indeed people with whom they can share such things and who understand them.

Daniel nevertheless emphasizes that one weekend will not change anyone's whole year if afterwards they do not invest in the areas they discovered. He gives examples: someone considers himself a believer his whole life, and realizes that he has never read the Bible on his own. Another earns well for the family, but realizes that at home he has children who need him, and he has no time for them precisely because he works. Such a person, Daniel suggests, could take his son on the weekend next time or draw closer to him in some other way.

sections.subtitle: Zašto jedan vikend nije dovoljan
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel Wurzberg prepričava razgovor sa sudionikom kojeg je nakon vikenda hvatala depresija
sections.content:
Daniel ističe da su važni i program s kontinuitetom, poput serijala koji traje tri mjeseca, i vikend koji za mnoge bude tek početak promišljanja. Na vikend ponekad dođu muškarci koji su događaj vidjeli na društvenim mrežama. Stignu *„k'o padobranci“*, bez ikakvih očekivanja, a onda se iznenade koliko im je nešto takvo nedostajalo.

Ispričao je i anegdotu sa sudionikom kojeg je prošle godine pitao hoće li opet doći. Muškarac mu je odgovorio da više neće. Vikend mu je bio jedan od najboljih u životu, ali nakon njega upao je u tešku depresiju jer se kod kuće ništa nije promijenilo. Daniel mu je odgovorio da je to zato što živi od vikenda do vikenda, a cijelu godinu između ne poduzima ništa. Kruno dodaje: *„Ne radiš na sebi.“*

Daniel u tome vidi **boljku muškaraca**: spremni su brzo zasukati rukave, ali im nedostaje ustrajnosti. Malo će se toga dogoditi preko noći, za jedan vikend ili tjedan predavanja. Uspoređuje to s treningom: *„Tko god je vježbao zna da u tjedan dana možeš samo pare potrošit.“* Uspjeh dolazi tek s dosljednošću. Tada čovjek otkriva čega se mora riješiti, u što mora uložiti i čemu se želi posvetiti.

Zato je potreban **ekosustav podrške**. To može biti, na primjer, WhatsApp grupa s trojicom prijatelja koji hrabre muškarca da ustraje. Takvo okruženje hrani njegovu odluku za bolje i pomaže mu da nastavi živjeti u skladu s njom. Kruno to sažima izrekom: *„S kim si, takav si.“*

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na ustrajnosti, svakodnevnom radu na sebi i podršci prijatelja uglavnom je u skladu s kršćanskim razumijevanjem rasta, koji je put, a ne jednokratno iskustvo; crkveno učenje pritom podsjeća da se na tom putu ne treba izolirati i da je ustrajnost također Božji dar.
concerns: Objašnjenje sudionikove teške depresije time što navodno nije radio na sebi može zvučati kao okrivljavanje i svesti složenu patnju na manjak truda; pastoralno je primjerenije priznati ozbiljnost depresije i ne pretpostaviti njezin uzrok.
Izraz „boljka muškaraca“ široko generalizira o muškarcima, a „S kim si, takav si“ ne treba shvatiti kao tvrdnju da okolina potpuno određuje čovjekov karakter.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska ustrajnost nije oslanjanje samo na vlastitu snagu: crkveni tekst naglašava potrebu za Božjom milošću, novim počecima i pratnjom prijatelja koji pomažu ostati vjeran na putu. Zato je ideja trajne podrške vrijedna, osobito ako zajednica potiče molitvu, odgovornost i traženje prikladne stručne pomoći kad je potrebna; vikend ili program mogu biti početak, ali ne jamče sami po sebi trajnu promjenu.
magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on perseverance, daily work on oneself, and the support of friends is largely in accordance with the Christian understanding of growth, which is a journey rather than a one-time experience; Church teaching simultaneously recalls that one should not isolate oneself on that journey and that perseverance is also a gift of God.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christian perseverance is not relying solely on one's own strength: Church text emphasizes the need for God's grace, new beginnings, and the accompaniment of friends who help one remain faithful on the path. Therefore, the idea of ongoing support is valuable, especially if the community fosters prayer, accountability, and seeking appropriate professional help when needed; a weekend or a program can be a beginning, but they do not in themselves guarantee lasting change.
concerns_en: The explanation of the participant's severe depression by the fact that he allegedly did not work on himself can sound like blaming and reduce complex suffering to a lack of effort; pastorally it is more appropriate to acknowledge the severity of depression and not assume its cause.
The phrase “men's ailment” broadly generalizes about men, and “With whom you are, such you are” should not be understood as a claim that the environment completely determines a person's character.

sections.subtitle_en: Why one weekend is not enough
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel Wurzberg recounts a conversation with a participant who was gripped by depression after the weekend
sections.content_en:
Daniel emphasizes that both a program with continuity, like a series lasting three months, and a weekend that for many is only the beginning of reflection, are important. Sometimes men come to the weekend who saw the event on social media. They arrive *“like paratroopers”*, without any expectations, and then they are surprised by how much they had missed something like that.

He also shared an anecdote with a participant whom he asked last year whether he would come again. The man answered him that he would not anymore. The weekend was one of the best in his life, but after it he fell into a severe depression because nothing had changed at home. Daniel answered him that it was because he lives from weekend to weekend, and does nothing during the entire year in between. Kruno adds: *“You are not working on yourself.”*

In this, Daniel sees **an ailment of men**: they are ready to roll up their sleeves quickly, but they lack perseverance. Little will happen overnight, in one weekend or a week of lectures. He compares it to training: *“Whoever has worked out knows that in a week you can only waste money.”* Success comes only with consistency. Then a man discovers what he must get rid of, what he must invest in, and what he wants to dedicate himself to.

That is why a **support ecosystem** is needed. This can be, for example, a WhatsApp group with three friends who encourage the man to persevere. Such an environment feeds his decision for the better and helps him continue living in accordance with it. Kruno summarizes this with the saying: *“With whom you are, such you are.”*

sections.subtitle: Redefinicija: brak i emocionalno zreo muškarac
sections.screenshot_description: Gost razmišlja o definiciji braka u blic pitanjima „Redefinicija“
sections.content:
Na kraju Kruno uvodi blic pitanja pod nazivom **„Redefinicija“**, u kojima od gosta traži definicije pojmova u jednoj rečenici.

**Kako bi definirao brak?** Daniel kratko razmisli, a zatim odgovori:

> *„Savez dvoje dobronamjernih ljudi koji žele stavit ovo drugo ispred.“*

Kruno odgovor prihvaća riječima: *„Stavit ćemo u rječnik.“*

**Što znači biti emocionalno zreo muškarac?** Daniel priznaje da bi se borio s tom definicijom i da je to tema koju i sam istražuje i o kojoj čita. Ističe da je ta zrelost povezana s poznavanjem sebe i spoznajom kako ga je Bog stvorio. Takav muškarac mora živjeti u skladu s onim kako je Bog zamislio život muškarca, uz pomoć Njegove riječi. Na kraju sažima: emocionalno zreo muškarac je **osoba koja se zna zrelo nositi sa situacijom**. To se odnosi na rješavanje sukoba i na preuzimanje odgovornosti za sebe, za svoje zdravlje, obitelj i djecu. Riječ je, kaže, o *„zrelosti koja preuzima odgovornost“*. Kruno odgovor ocjenjuje kao „savršen“.

magisterium.assessment: Opis uglavnom odgovara kršćanskom naglasku na uzajamnom darivanju, vjernosti i odgovornosti, a posebno je pozitivno što emocionalnu zrelost povezuje sa samospoznajom, rješavanjem sukoba i odgovornošću za obitelj. Ipak, definicija braka ostaje nepotpuna: ne spominje da je brak trajni savez muškarca i žene niti njegovo sakramentalno obilježje, a izraz „staviti drugo ispred” može tražiti pojašnjenje da se uzajamno darivanje ne poistovjećuje sa zanemarivanjem sebe.
concerns: Definicija braka kao saveza „dvoje dobronamjernih ljudi” ne ističe spolnu narav bračne zajednice muškarca i žene, njezinu trajnost ni sakramentalni karakter; kao kratka, neformalna definicija zato je teološki nepotpuna.

„Staviti drugo ispred” može dobro izraziti nesebičnu ljubav, ali bez uzajamnosti i razboritosti može zvučati kao jednostrano samoponištavanje. Kršćansko bračno darivanje jest uzajamno i treba poštovati dostojanstvo obaju supružnika.

Poziv muškarcu da živi prema Božjem naumu ostaje neodređen; važno je da se ne tumači kao kruta stereotipna podjela uloga koja zanemaruje osobno dostojanstvo, slobodu i uzajamnu odgovornost supružnika. Dostavljeni odlomak ne razrađuje što točno pod tim podrazumijeva.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje braka nadilazi dobru namjeru: riječ je o trajnom, vjernom i potpunom uzajamnom darivanju koje u kršćanskom braku postaje sakramentalni znak Kristove ljubavi prema Crkvi. Sveto pismo i crkveno tumačenje povezuju bračnu zrelost s uzajamnim poštovanjem, nesebičnom ljubavlju, rješavanjem sukoba i stalnim obnavljanjem bračnog obećanja. Zato je naglasak na odgovornosti dobar, a izraz „staviti drugo ispred” najtočnije se razumije kao obostrano služenje u ljubavi, uz pomoć Božje milosti, a ne kao ukidanje vlastitog dostojanstva ili potreba.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description generally corresponds to the Christian emphasis on mutual self-giving, fidelity, and responsibility, and it is particularly positive that it links emotional maturity with self-knowledge, conflict resolution, and responsibility for the family. Nevertheless, the definition of marriage remains incomplete: it does not mention that marriage is a permanent covenant of a man and a woman, nor its sacramental character, and the expression "put the other first" may require clarification so that mutual self-giving is not equated with neglecting oneself.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of marriage goes beyond good intention: it is a permanent, faithful, and total mutual self-giving that in Christian marriage becomes a sacramental sign of Christ's love for the Church. Sacred Scripture and ecclesial interpretation associate marital maturity with mutual respect, selfless love, conflict resolution, and the constant renewal of the marital promise. Therefore, the emphasis on responsibility is good, and the expression "put the other first" is most accurately understood as mutual service in love, with the help of God's grace, and not as the abolition of one's own dignity or needs.
concerns_en: The definition of marriage as a covenant of "two well-intentioned people" does not emphasize the sexual nature of the marital union of a man and a woman, its permanence, nor its sacramental character; as a short, informal definition, it is therefore theologically incomplete.

"Put the other first" can well express selfless love, but without reciprocity and prudence it can sound like unilateral self-effacement. Christian marital self-giving is mutual and must respect the dignity of both spouses.

The call for a man to live according to God's plan remains indeterminate; it is important that it is not interpreted as a rigid stereotypical division of roles that disregards personal dignity, freedom, and the mutual responsibility of spouses. The provided excerpt does not elaborate what exactly is meant by that.

sections.subtitle_en: Redefinition: marriage and an emotionally mature man
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest reflects on the definition of marriage in the lightning questions "Redefinition"
sections.content_en:
At the end, Kruno introduces lightning questions titled **"Redefinition"**, in which he asks the guest for one-sentence definitions of concepts.

**How would you define marriage?** Daniel thinks briefly, and then replies:

> *"A covenant of two well-intentioned people who want to put the other first."*

Kruno accepts the answer with the words: *"We will put it in the dictionary."*

**What does it mean to be an emotionally mature man?** Daniel admits that he would struggle with that definition and that it is a topic he himself explores and reads about. He emphasizes that this maturity is connected with knowing oneself and understanding how God created him. Such a man must live in accordance with how God envisioned the life of a man, with the help of His word. In the end, he summarizes: an emotionally mature man is **a person who knows how to deal maturely with a situation**. This refers to resolving conflicts and taking responsibility for oneself, for one's health, family, and children. It is about, he says, *"maturity that takes responsibility"*. Kruno rates the answer as "perfect".

sections.subtitle: Izazov za gledatelje: umjesto kritike ponudite rješenje
sections.screenshot_description: Daniel Wurzberg poziva gledatelje da uz svaku zamjerku ponude konkretno rješenje
sections.content:
Posljednje pitanje odnosi se na izazov koji bi gost uputio gledateljima, i muškarcima i ženama, za sljedeći tjedan u njihovoj vezi ili braku.

Daniel predlaže sljedeće. Ako u odnosu postoji nešto što partnere jako žulja, bilo da je novijeg datuma ili traje dugo, neka odvoje vrijeme da smisle **kreativan način na koji bi to riješili**. Tako iritacija ne bi postala *„samo hrana za kritiku“*, nego bi donijela rješenje.

Njegova je poruka jednostavna: **ako imaš nešto za prigovoriti, ponudi i rješenje**. Ono ne mora biti ispravno, ali osoba tada dolazi za stol s porukom: *„Želim raditi na našem odnosu, ovo me smetalo, evo jedne moje ideje.“* Daniel vjeruje da to otvara vrata napretku. Suprotan pristup sažima rečenicom: *„Meni ovo ide na živce, a ti si kriv.“*

Kruno zaključuje da treba biti konkretan i namjeran te sam preuzeti inicijativu.

magisterium.assessment: Poticanje da se prigovor iznese konstruktivno, uz spremnost na osobnu inicijativu i rad za dobro odnosa, uglavnom je u skladu s kršćanskim shvaćanjem braka kao trajnog zajedničkog poziva na rast i rješavanje nesuglasica. Ipak, prijedlog rješenja ne bi smio zamijeniti strpljivo slušanje niti značiti da je osoba koja iznosi problem dužna sama ga riješiti.
concerns: Ako bi se izreka „ako imaš nešto za prigovoriti, ponudi i rješenje” primjenjivala kao strogo pravilo, mogla bi nepravedno opteretiti onoga tko trpi problem ili obeshrabriti iskreno izražavanje boli. Bračni dijalog ponekad traži prije svega da se druga osoba sasluša i da se njezina bol prizna, a ne da se odmah ponudi rješenje.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva opisuje bračni život kao dinamičan zajednički zadatak: supružnici trebaju uzajamno preuzimati odgovornost, poštovati jedno drugo i nastojati razriješiti sukobe, a ne svesti odnos na optuživanje. Papa Franjo upozorava da trajna kritičnost šteti bračnoj zajednici, ali istodobno naglašava strpljivo slušanje i pažljiv izbor riječi; zato je dobar prijedlog rješenja početak suradničkog razgovora, a ne uvjet da bi netko smio iznijeti svoju teškoću.

magisterium.assessment_en: Encouraging that an objection be presented constructively, with a readiness for personal initiative and work for the good of the relationship, is generally in accordance with the Christian understanding of marriage as an enduring shared call to growth and the resolving of disagreements. Nevertheless, proposing a solution should not replace patient listening, nor should it mean that the person raising the issue is obligated to solve it on their own.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church describes married life as a dynamic shared task: spouses need to mutually assume responsibility, respect one another, and strive to resolve conflicts, rather than reducing the relationship to accusation. Pope Francis warns that persistent fault-finding harms marital communion, yet at the same time he emphasizes patient listening and a careful choice of words; therefore, a good proposed solution is the beginning of a collaborative conversation, not a condition for someone to be allowed to express their difficulty.
concerns_en: If the saying "if you have something to complain about, offer a solution as well" were applied as a strict rule, it could unjustly burden the one who suffers the problem or discourage the sincere expression of pain. Marital dialogue sometimes requires, above all, that the other person be listened to and that their pain be acknowledged, rather than a solution being offered immediately.

sections.subtitle_en: Challenge for viewers: offer a solution instead of criticism
sections.screenshot_description_en: Daniel Wurzberg invites viewers to offer a concrete solution alongside every objection
sections.content_en:
The last question pertains to a challenge that the guest would address to viewers, both men and women, for the coming week in their relationship or marriage.

Daniel suggests the following. If there is something in the relationship that bothers the partners intensely, whether it is of recent date or has lasted a long time, let them set aside time to come up with **a creative way in which they would solve it**. That way, irritation would not become *"merely food for criticism"*, but would bring about a solution.

His message is simple: **if you have something to complain about, offer a solution as well**. It does not have to be correct, but the person then comes to the table with the message: *"I want to work on our relationship, this was bothering me, here is one idea of mine."* Daniel believes that this opens the door to progress. He summarizes the opposite approach with the sentence: *"This gets on my nerves, and it's your fault."*

Kruno concludes that one needs to be concrete and intentional, and take the initiative oneself.

sections.subtitle: Za deset godina? „U Božjoj milosti, kao i do sad“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost odgovara na posljednje pitanje gdje se vidi za deset godina
sections.content:
Kruno zahvaljuje Danielu što je *„probio led“* u prvoj epizodi podcasta i izražava nadu da će se opet susresti. Gledatelje poziva na dijeljenje, lajkanje i pretplatu, *„kako se to lijepo kaže na starohrvatskom“*, te najavljuje sljedeću Redefiniciju za mjesec dana. Dodaje da članovi **Patreon** kanala već danas mogu pogledati drugu epizodu podcasta.

Nakon odjave slijedi još jedno pitanje: **gdje se gost vidi za deset godina?**

Daniel odgovara mirno: *„U Božjoj milosti, kao i do sad.“* Kaže da i dalje planira biti voljeni sin kojeg će Bog uvijek *„primiti za kragnu“* i staviti na pravo mjesto u pravo vrijeme. Zaključuje: *„To je sve što mi u životu treba. Sve drugo može otići.“*

magisterium.assessment: Danielov odgovor uglavnom je usklađen s katoličkim povjerenjem u Božju milost i providnost: izražava zahvalnost za Božje vodstvo i pouzdanje u budućnost, a ne samodostatnost. Izraz da sve drugo može otići može značiti kršćansku nevezanost, ali bez dodatnog konteksta nije jasno isključuje li time i važne životne odgovornosti.
concerns: Slika Boga koji ga prima za kragnu i stavlja na pravo mjesto može se razumjeti kao slikovit izraz pouzdanja, ali ne bi je trebalo tumačiti kao tvrdnju da Bog prisilno upravlja čovjekom.
Rečenica da sve drugo može otići može izražavati predanje Bogu, no ne bi smjela značiti zanemarivanje dužnosti prema bližnjima ili obveza koje proizlaze iz njegova životnog poziva.
magisterium.enrichment: Katekizam opisuje povjerenje u Boga kao pouzdanje u svakoj okolnosti, pa i u nevolji, a papinsko učenje povezuje povjerenje u milost s time da postanemo kanali milosrđa drugima. Zato kršćansko predanje nije nužno pasivnost ili odbacivanje svega stvorenoga: ono može značiti da se vlastiti planovi podređuju Bogu, dok se vjerno živi ono što nam je povjereno.

magisterium.assessment_en: Daniel's answer is largely aligned with Catholic trust in God's grace and providence: it expresses gratitude for God's guidance and confidence in the future, rather than self-sufficiency. The expression that everything else can go may signify Christian detachment, but without additional context it is not clear whether it thereby also excludes important life responsibilities.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catechism describes trust in God as confidence in every circumstance, even in adversity, and papal teaching links trust in grace with becoming channels of mercy to others. Therefore, Christian surrender is not necessarily passivity or a rejection of all created things: it can mean that one's own plans are subordinated to God, while faithfully living out what has been entrusted to us.
concerns_en: The image of God grabbing him by the collar and putting him in the right place can be understood as a figurative expression of trust, but it should not be interpreted as a claim that God forcefully controls man.
The sentence that everything else can go may express surrender to God, but it should not mean neglecting duties toward one's neighbors or obligations arising from his vocation in life.

sections.subtitle_en: In ten years? "In God's grace, as until now"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest answers the final question of where he sees himself in ten years
sections.content_en:
Kruno thanks Daniel for having *„broken the ice“* in the first episode of the podcast and expresses hope that they will meet again. He invites viewers to share, like, and subscribe, *„as they nicely say in Old Croatian“*, and announces the next Redefinicija in a month. He adds that members of the **Patreon** channel can watch the second episode of the podcast as early as today.

After the sign-off, another question follows: **where does the guest see himself in ten years?**

Daniel answers calmly: *„In God's grace, as until now.“* He says that he still plans to be a beloved son whom God will always *„grab by the collar“* and put in the right place at the right time. He concludes: *„That is all I need in life. Everything else can go.“*
